Taiwan Indigenous farmer revives climate-resilient millet - The Japan Times
Taiwan Indigenous farmer revives climate-resilient millet
Farmers Linkav Ismahasan (left) and Banu Ismahasan harvest oil millet in a field in Taitung, Taiwan, on Oct. 21. Once grown by Indigenous farmers in Taiwan in case their staple crops died, oil millet largely disappeared from fields more than 60 years ago as rice became more available. | AFP-JIJI
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link
Taiwan – Indigenous farmer Banu Ismahasan walks through a golden field of tall stalks in southeastern Taiwan, harvesting by hand the grain heads of an ancient crop resistant to extreme weather.
Once grown by Indigenous farmers in Taiwan in case their staple crops died, oil millet largely disappeared from fields more than 60 years ago as rice became more available.
Over the past decade, Ismahasan and his elderly parents have worked to revive the nearly forgotten crop in the Bunun community in Buklavu, a village surrounded by lush green mountains in Taitung county.
“We just hope to bring back many traditional Bunun crops and grow them on this land again,” Ismahasan, 48, said in his oil millet field under a clear blue sky.
Oil millet, or dill in the Bunun language, is endemic to Taiwan and can be found growing wild in the mountains.
Ismahasan first read about the plant online and then embarked on his own research, combing through historical documents and speaking to tribal elders, including a woman who recalled last eating it half a century ago.
He discovered that Bunun farmers used to grow oil millet alongside their staple crop foxtail millet as a “back-up” when harvests failed or disasters hit.
After years of growing oil millet himself, Ismahasan came to understand why his ancestors relied on the crop.
A single oil millet seed can grow 15 to 20 panicles, or branching seed clusters, and the stems regenerate on their own, while foxtail millet typically grows one panicle per seed and must be sown again after being cut.
It has also proven hardier than foxtail millet when extreme weather or disease outbreaks have ravaged his 2.2-hectare 5.4-acre farm.
During a drought several years ago that lasted more than 200 days, the oil millet “stayed bright green” while other crops withered, Ismahasan said.
Typhoons, floods and even a rust disease outbreak have not affected it either.
Hsing Yue-ie, a retired professor from Taiwan’s Academia Sinica and an expert in plant genetics, first heard of oil millet 15 years ago at an international forum.
Unbeknownst to Hsing, specimens of Taiwan oil millet collected in the 1890s were sitting in Britain’s Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew.
Hsing led a research team to find oil millet in the mountains of southeastern Taiwan and began studying the little-known cereal.
Farmer Banu Ismahasan spreads freshly harvested oil millet out to dry in the sun in Taitung, Taiwan, on Oct. 21. | AFP-JIJI
She found that the seed’s protective wax coating enabled it to grow without irrigation, fertilizers or pesticides, even on poor-quality land.
Rich in oil, protein and minerals, it can be used for human and animal consumption, as well as for fuel.
“It’s naturally very efficient at using sunlight and water,” said Hsing.
“As for soil conditions, even in mountainous areas where the ground is full of large rocks, it can still grow very well.”
Ismahasan started his crop with one panicle of oil millet. The family now harvests oil millet twice a year on a section of their property where they grow other traditional Bunun cereal crops.
Tiny and tasteless, oil millet can be used in porridge, steamed buns, bread and even popcorn.
But the family has struggled to convince other farmers to grow it because it is not yet commercially viable.
Oil millet is not only labor intensive but also significantly more expensive for consumers than rice, by far Taiwan’s most popular staple.
While the current market for oil millet is limited, Taiwan’s National Crop Germplasm Center sees value in preserving its seeds for the future, when climate change might force more farmers to consider growing the crop.
Oil millet seeds are “very precious” because of their genetic diversity and ability to adapt to the environment, said Lin Yen-yu, an assistant researcher at the center.
Seeds are kept in aluminum foil packets and stored at minus 18 degrees Celsius under low-moisture conditions where they can last for decades, Lin said.
“In the future, when cultivation methods or climate change undergo certain shifts, their value may start to be recognized and discovered,” he said. “It preserves many possibilities.”
Ismahasan said his priority for now was to get more people in his community growing and eating oil millet, bringing “it back into our everyday lives, just as it was for our elders.”
“If we don’t even eat it ourselves anymore, how can we expect to turn it into a viable business?” he said.

summary: 东盟保留对缅甸的限制，但开辟政治回归之路 - 日本时报 东盟保留缅甸限制，但开辟政治回归之路 菲律宾总统小费迪南德·马科斯（右）和新加坡总理黄循财周日出席在马尼拉举行的东盟领导人交流会。 | POOL/来自法新社-JIJI X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads 电子邮件 打印 书签故事 复制链接 马尼拉 - 东南亚领导人周日表示，如果缅甸在其长期目标上取得进展，他们可能会考虑逐步恢复缅甸在该地区集团的全面政治代表权

东盟保留缅甸限制，但开辟政治回归之路 - 日本时报
东盟保留对缅甸的限制，但为政治回归开辟道路
菲律宾总统小费迪南德·马科斯（右）和新加坡总理黄循财周日出席在马尼拉举行的东盟领导人交流会。 |泳池 / 法新社-JIJI
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads 电子邮件 打印 书签故事 复制链接
马尼拉 - 东南亚领导人周日表示，如果缅甸在解决五年危机的长期计划上取得进展，他们可能会考虑逐步恢复缅甸在该地区集团的全面政治代表权。
东南亚国家联盟 11 个成员国的领导人在马尼拉峰会上同意维持目前将缅甸排除在东盟峰会和外长会议上的全面政治代表权的政策。
但他们表示，如果缅甸在欧盟提出的计划（即五点共识或5PC）上取得“持续和具体”进展，他们同意通过“分阶段和基于进展”的方式进行“有针对性的接触”。
值得注意的是，该集团似乎还支持其成员国与缅甸进行双边接触。
近几个月来，泰国和其他几个东盟成员国加强了与缅甸的接触，给东盟带来了新的压力，要求其放宽对缅甸军方支持的领导人参加高级别会议的禁令。
领导人在峰会上通过的一项联合决定中表示：“如果缅甸在落实五项原则方面取得持续和具体进展，东盟可能会考虑逐步恢复缅甸的全面政治代表性。”
他们表示：“我们还鼓励东盟各成员国与所有相关利益攸关方进行建设性接触，并与东盟主席协商，推动 5PC 的实施取得实质性进展。”
2021 年缅甸军方夺取政权后不久，东盟就通过了五点共识，呼吁立即停止当地暴力，并在各方之间启动建设性对话。它提供东盟调解和人道主义援助。
缅甸军队支持的政府希望与东盟实现关系正常化。自从军方推翻诺贝尔和平奖获得者昂山素季的民选政府以来，该国一直处于动荡之中，引发了一场内战，联合国估计这场内战已造成 10 万人死亡，超过 350 万人流离失所。
政变领导人、现任总统敏昂莱的军队得到了中国、印度和俄罗斯的支持。近几个月来，他的政府获得了越来越多的国际认可，包括在唐纳德·特朗普总统的政府扭转多年的孤立状态时与美国官员进行秘密会谈。

ASEAN keeps Myanmar restrictions but opens path to political return - The Japan Times
ASEAN keeps Myanmar restrictions but opens path to political return
Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. (right) and Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong attend the ASEAN Leaders Interface in Manila on Sunday. | POOL / via AFP-JIJI
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link
Manila – Southeast Asian leaders said on Sunday they may ​consider gradually restoring Myanmar’s full political representation in the regional bloc, if ‌the country makes ‌progress on their longstanding plan to resolve its five-year-old crisis.
Leaders ​of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations agreed at a summit in Manila to maintain their policy of excluding Myanmar from full political representation at ASEAN summits ⁠and foreign ministers’ meetings for now.
But they said they had agreed to pursue a “calibrated engagement” ⁠through a “phased and progress-based” approach, if Myanmar makes “sustained and concrete” progress on the bloc’s proposed plan, known as the five-point consensus, or 5PC.
And ​in a notable step, the bloc ⁠also appeared to endorse bilateral outreach to Myanmar among its member countries.
Thailand and several other ASEAN members have stepped ⁠up engagement with Myanmar ​in recent months, creating new pressureon the bloc to ease ​its ban on Myanmar’s military-backed leaders attending its high-level meetings.
“Subject to ​sustained and ‌concrete progress in the implementation of the 5PC by Myanmar, ASEAN may consider the gradual restoration of Myanmar’s full political representation,” the leaders said in a joint decision adopted at the summit.
“We also encourage efforts by individual ASEAN ‌Member States through constructive engagement with all relevant stakeholders, in consultation with the ASEAN Chair, to advance substantive progress in the implementation of the 5PC,” they said.
ASEAN’s five-point consensus, adopted soon after the military seized power in Myanmar in 2021, calls for an immediate end ​to ​violence there and for the launch of constructive dialogue among ​all parties. It offers ASEAN mediation and humanitarian assistance.
Myanmar’s army-backed government wants to normalise ⁠ties with ASEAN. The country has been in turmoil since the military ousted Nobel Peace Prize winner Aung San Suu Kyi’s elected government, triggering a civil war that the U.N. estimates has killed 100,000 people and displaced more than ​3.5 million.
Coup leader-turned-president Min Aung Hlaing’s military has received support from China, India and Russia. His administration has gained increasing international recognition in recent months, including secret talks with U.S. officials as President Donald Trump’s administration reverses years of isolation.

content:
出于安全考虑，无人机所有权禁令在北京生效 - 日本时报
出于安全考虑，北京实施无人机所有权禁令
10月26日，一面中国国旗在北京中央商务区的摩天大楼前飘扬。路透社
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads 电子邮件 打印 书签故事 复制链接
北京——北京禁止拥有无人机的禁令于周日生效，当局称这项措施将有助于确保中国首都的安全。
该禁令适用于该市面积约 16,400 平方公里（大约是比利时面积一半）的城市化和农村地区。
北京于九月宣布的这项禁令禁止拥有和储存无人驾驶飞行器（UAV），以“维护首都安全”。
还禁止将无人机或其组件运输到城市。
在周日实施之前，业主被迫扔掉他们的设备，要么在批准的回购点或在网上转售。
他们也可以将他们运送到执法区域之外。
北京是中国中央政府、最高领导人和执政的中国共产党总部的所在地，面临着严格的安全措施。
6 月份，一架小型飞机撞向该市最高的摩天大楼，造成飞行员死亡、另有 13 人受伤，引发了空域安全担忧，随后出台了这项禁令。
北京已于 2026 年 5 月禁止无人机销售，业主被要求向当局注册其设备，但可以保留它们。
现在，任何拥有无人机的人都可能面临罚款并没收其设备。
出于反恐、执法、紧急救援、农业或科学研究等特定原因，可能会给予无人机飞行豁免。
近年来，无人机在中国变得非常流行，特别是在拍摄风景方面。

Drone ownership ban comes into force in Beijing over security concerns - The Japan Times
Drone ownership ban comes into force in Beijing over security concerns
A Chinese national flag flies in front of skyscrapers of Beijing's Central Business District on Oct. 26. | REUTERS
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link
Beijing – Beijing’s ban on possessing drones came into force Sunday, a measure authorities said will help ensure the security of China’s capital city.
The ban applies to both urbanized and rural areas in the municipality of around 16,400 square kilometers — an area roughly half the size of Belgium.
The ban, which Beijing announced in September, outlaws owning and storing uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) to “safeguard the security of the capital.”
Transporting drones or their components into the city was also forbidden.
Owners had been forced to get rid of their devices ahead of Sunday’s implementation, either by reselling them at approved buy-back points or online.
They could also have transported them outside the enforcement area.
Beijing, home to China’s central government, top leaders and the headquarters of the ruling Chinese Communist Party (CCP), has faced strict security measures.
The ban comes after airspace safety fears were raised in June when a small plane crashed into the city’s tallest skyscraper, killing the pilot and injuring 13 others.
Beijing had already banned drone sales in May 2026, with owners required to register their devices with authorities but permitted to keep them.
Now, anyone in possession of a drone could face a fine and the confiscation of their equipment.
Exemptions for drone flights may be granted for specific reasons such as counterterrorism, law enforcement, emergency relief, agriculture or scientific research.
Drones have become extremely popular in China in recent years, particularly for filming landscapes.

伊朗称袭击了美国基地，巴林发布自九月以来的首次威胁警报 - 日本时报
伊朗称袭击了美国基地，巴林发布自 9 月以来的首次威胁警报
周四，在德黑兰郊外的国家航空航天公园举行的导弹和无人机展览上，孩子们站在地对空导弹系统上。 |法新社-即时
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads 电子邮件 打印 书签故事 复制链接
巴林周日发布了两份潜在威胁警报，这是自去年 9 月以来首次发出此类警告，伊朗表示，由于美伊旨在结束近 9 个月战争的协议存在不确定性，因此袭击了位于海湾国家的美国基地。
据伊朗法尔斯通讯社报道，伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队表示，他们袭击了巴林的一个美国军事基地，以报复“美国的敌对行动”。
当地时间凌晨 4 点左右可以听到爆炸声，居民报告早上 6 点 30 分左右发生了第二轮爆炸。
据伊朗国营新闻电视台报道，革命卫队表示，他们已发射六架无人机，瞄准巴林 Al-Rifaa 直升机基地的美国防空雷达。美国或巴林当局没有立即证实这一消息。
巴林是美国海军第五舰队的所在地，巴林内政部表示，敦促公民和居民保持冷静，前往最近的安全地点。它没有提供有关威胁的更多细节。
两天前，革命卫队表示，他们袭击了位于巴林的美国预警雷达。美国军方否认了这一说法，称其拦截了两架伊朗无人机，没有造成任何损坏。
结束冲突的外交努力尚未取得突破，尽管华盛顿和德黑兰推迟了战争中的直接攻击，这场战争始于2月28日美国和以色列对伊朗的袭击，随后蔓延到整个地区，德黑兰向海湾国家的美国基地发射导弹和无人机袭击。
唐纳德·特朗普总统最近几天表示，如果美国不再面临来自德黑兰或伊朗支持的也门胡塞武装的新挑衅，他可能会推迟攻击伊朗，但他将维持美国的海上封锁。
然而，在另一条战线上，胡塞武装和沙特领导的打击他们的联盟继续相互攻击，该联盟周日表示，它拦截了两枚胡塞武装向沙特首都利雅得发射的弹道导弹，并在沙特石油资源丰富的东部省拦截了三架无人机。

Bahrain issues first threat alerts since September as Iran says it attacked U.S. base
Children stand on a surface-to-air missile system displayed at an exhibition of missiles and drones at the National Aerospace Park outside Tehran on Thursday. | AFP-JIJI
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link
Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats Sunday, its first such warnings since September, as Iran said it had attacked a U.S. base in the Gulf country amid uncertainty over a U.S.-Iran deal aimed at ending the nearly 9-month-old war.
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it had attacked a U.S. military base in Bahrain in retaliation for “hostile U.S. actions,” Iran’s Fars news agency reported.
Explosions could be heard around 4 a.m. local time, with residents reporting a second series of blasts around 6:30 a.m.
The Revolutionary Guard said they had launched six drones targeting a U.S. air-defense radar at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base in Bahrain, Iranian state-run Press TV reported. There was no immediate confirmation from U.S. or Bahraini authorities.
Bahrain, home to the U.S. Navy’s 5th Fleet, urged citizens and residents to remain calm and proceed to the nearest safe location, the interior ministry said. It did not provide further details on the threats.
Two days earlier the Revolutionary Guard said they had attacked a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain. The U.S. military denied this, saying it had intercepted two Iranian drones without any damage.
Diplomatic efforts to end the conflict have yet to produce a breakthrough, though Washington and Tehran have held off on direct attacks in the war that began with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb. 28 and then spread across the region, with Tehran launching missile and drone attacks on U.S. bases in Gulf countries.
President Donald Trump has said in recent days that he might hold off on attacking Iran if the U.S. faces no new provocations from Tehran or the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, but that he would maintain a U.S. naval blockade.
On another front, however, the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition fighting them have continued to exchange attacks, with the coalition saying on Sunday it had intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles launched toward the Saudi capital Riyadh and three drones in the kingdom’s oil-rich Eastern Province.

content:
资助机会通知 (NOFO)：在斯威士兰举办 2027 GCTF 研讨会 资助机会通知 (NOFO) 在斯威士兰美国台湾学院举办 2027 G CTF 研讨会 机会编号：GCTF-TAIPEI-FY2 7 -00 1 申请截止日期：202 年 11 月 23 日 6 日晚上 11:59 （台北时间） A. 基本信息 1. 概述 资助方式：合作协议。合作协议包括局或大使馆实质性参与项目的计划实施。实质性参与的例子包含在下面的 C.2 节中。项目实施期限：拟建项目应于202年5月31日前完成 7．本通知视资金情况而定。公共外交部门保留在被认为符合美国政府最佳利益的情况下授予少于或超过所述资金的权利，具体取决于资金的可用性和指定拨款官员的批准。 2. 执行摘要 美国在台协会 (AIT) 公共外交部门 (PDS) 宣布开展一项合作协议公开竞赛，以支持 2027 年第一季度或第二季度在斯威士兰规划和实施全球合作与培训框架 (GCTF) 区域特许经营研讨会。在资金允许的情况下，AIT 打算授予一份约 20 万美元的合作协议来实施该计划。
全球合作与培训框架（GCTF）是一个国际能力建设平台，汇集了政府官员、技术专家、行业代表、学者和民间社会代表，交流实践经验并加强应对区域和全球挑战的合作。GCTF由台湾和美国于2015年成立，此后扩大到包括日本、澳大利亚、加拿大和英国作为合作伙伴。拟议的研讨会“加强南部非洲的网络安全和数字治理”预计将于 2027 年第一季度或第二季度在斯威士兰举行。该计划将重点关注加强网络安全弹性、改善数字治理、保护关键数字基础设施、应对新出现的网络威胁以及促进安全和可信的数字转型。它将为参与者提供一个交流实践经验、确定共同挑战、加强专业网络和区域合作的平台。该研讨会预计将包括来自至少八个非洲国家的代表，特别强调南部非洲的区域参与。第一天预计将有约 60 至 80 名参与者参加，活动内容包括全体讨论、专家演讲和实践交流。

Executive Summary The American Institute in Taiwan (AIT) Public Diplomacy Section (PDS) announces an open competition for a cooperative agreement to support the planning and implementation of a Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) regional franchise workshop in Eswatini in the first or second quarter of 2027. Subject to the availability of funding, AIT intends to award one cooperative agreement of approximately USD 200,000 to implement this program. The Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) is an international capacity-building platform that brings together government officials, technical experts, industry representatives, academics, and civil society representatives to exchange practical experiences and strengthen cooperation in addressing regional and global challenges. The GCTF was established by Taiwan and the United States in 2015 and has since expanded to include Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom as Partners. The proposed workshop, “Strengthening Cybersecurity and Digital Governance in Southern Africa,” is expected to take place in Eswatini during the first or second quarter of 2027. The program will focus on strengthening cybersecurity resilience, improving digital governance, protecting critical digital infrastructure, addressing emerging cyber threats, and promoting secure and trusted digital transformation. It will provide a platform for participants to exchange practical experiences, identify common challenges, and strengthen professional networks and regional cooperation. The workshop is expected to include representatives from at least eight African countries, with a particular emphasis on regional participation from Southern Africa. Approximately 60 to 80 participants are expected to participate in the first day of the program, which will feature plenary discussions, expert presentations, and practical exchanges. A smaller group of approximately 40 participants is expected to participate in the second day, which may include focused technical discussions, interactive exercises, working-group sessions, and/or relevant site visits. The program is expected to bring together government officials, cybersecurity and digital governance practitioners, technical experts, private-sector representatives, academics, civil society representatives, and other relevant stakeholders from participating African countries. Subject-matter experts from the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF Partners, including Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom, may also be invited to contribute relevant international expertise and practical experience. The selected recipient will serve as AIT’s implementation partner and will be responsible for comprehensive program and logistical support, including venue and lodging coordination, participant management, travel arrangements for designated participants and speakers, ground transportation, interpretation and audiovisual services, workshop materials, vendor coordination, monitoring and evaluation, and required grant reporting. Travel expenses for U.S. Government officials invited by the U.S. Government and Taiwan-supported speakers will be funded separately and should not be included in the recipient’s proposed budget. AIT and GCTF partners will provide overall policy guidance, strategic direction, and substantive oversight throughout program planning and implementation. Eligible applicants include nonprofit organizations, educational institutions, professional associations, think tanks, private-sector organizations with relevant international program management experience, public international organizations where eligible under applicable U.S. Government regulations, and other eligible organizations with demonstrated capacity to organize international conferences or capacity-building programs and administer U.S. Government assistance awards. This cooperative agreement is intended to strengthen practical cybersecurity capacity and digital governance cooperation in Southern Africa, expand professional and institutional connections among participating countries, and advance the GCTF as a platform for practical international capacity building, technical exchange, and sustained regional cooperation. Program Description 1. Project Background, Goals, and Objectives Project Background The Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) is an international capacity-building platform established by Taiwan and the United States in 2015. Japan joined as a full partner in 2019, followed by Australia in 2021, Canada in 2023, and the United Kingdom in 2025. Through workshops and other capacity-building activities, GCTF brings together government officials, technical experts, industry representatives, and civil society representatives to exchange practical experience, strengthen professional networks, and develop approaches to shared regional and global challenges. As governments and societies become increasingly dependent on digital technologies and interconnected systems, cybersecurity and effective digital governance have become important elements of economic development, public-service delivery, critical infrastructure resilience, and public trust. Recent research documents that scam syndicates displaced from Southeast Asian epicenters, including Myanmar, Laos, and Cambodia, are actively pivoting to Africa, with documented raids in nine African countries and growing evidence of scam infrastructure, including online gambling platforms used as cover for fraud operations, gray business Telegram groups openly advertising scam facilities, and unregulated cryptocurrency services establishing footholds across the continent. Countries across Southern Africa face evolving cybersecurity and cybercrime challenges while also seeking to expand digital services, strengthen institutional capacity, and develop governance frameworks that support secure and trusted digital transformation. The proposed GCTF regional workshop in Eswatini will provide a platform for government officials, cybersecurity and the digital governance practitioners, technical experts, private-sector representatives, academics, civil society representatives, and other relevant stakeholders from across Africa to exchange practical experiences and strengthen professional and institutional connections. The workshop is expected to include representatives from at least eight African countries, with particular emphasis on participation from Southern Africa. The program will draw on expertise and practical experience from participating African countries as well as the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF partners, as appropriate. Through expert presentations, policy and technical discussions, interactive exchanges, and other practical activities, the workshop will address shared challenges and identify approaches that participating countries may adapt to their respective national and institutional contexts. Strengthening cybersecurity capacity and secure digital governance in Southern Africa also advances U.S. security and economic interests. Cyber threats, cyber-enabled crime, and vulnerabilities in interconnected digital systems increasingly cross-national borders and can affect American citizens, businesses, and critical infrastructure. By strengthening the ability of partner countries to prevent, identify, respond to, and recover from cyber threats, this program can help reduce vulnerabilities that may be exploited by transnational criminal networks and other malicious cyber actors. The workshop will also strengthen U.S. engagement with African partners on secure and resilient digital ecosystems, promote cooperation and information sharing among governments and technical experts, and expand relationships between African stakeholders and the United States and other GCTF partners. Through practical capacity building and sustained professional networks, the program will support a more secure and resilient regional digital environment while advancing shared interests in cybersecurity, economic security, and trusted digital development. Project Goal: The goal of this project is to strengthen cybersecurity resilience and digital governance capacity in Southern Africa by facilitating practical knowledge exchange, regional cooperation, and sustained professional engagement among participating countries and international partners, while advancing shared U.S. and partner interests in a more secure, resilient, and trusted digital environment. Project Objectives: The project will pursue the following objectives: Strengthen Cybersecurity Capacity and Resilience: Enhance participants’ knowledge of practical approaches to preventing, preparing for, responding to, and recovering from cybersecurity threats and incidents, with a specific focus on basic cyber hygiene, national cyber resilience, digital trust, and the development of a secure digital ecosystem aligned with global standards and best practices. Advance Effective and Secure Digital Governance: Promote the exchange of policies, practices, institutional approaches, and lessons learned that support secure, trusted, resilient, and inclusive digital governance and digital transformation. Promote Regional Cooperation and Information Sharing: Strengthen professional and institutional connections among participating African countries and encourage greater cross-border cooperation, information sharing, and coordination in addressing shared cybersecurity and digital governance challenges. Facilitate Practical International Exchange: Connect African policymakers and practitioners with relevant expertise and practical experience from participating African countries, the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF partner countries, including Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom, as appropriate to the workshop agenda. Support Sustainable Professional Networks and Follow-on Cooperation: Encourage participants to identify practical opportunities for continued professional engagement, knowledge sharing, and future cooperation beyond the workshop. 2. Finally, the proposal aligns with the following: The project clearly demonstrates a direct contribution to current U.S. foreign policy priorities. The project will positively impact America’s reputation among foreign government partners. The project will positively impact American’s reputation among foreign publics. The proposal does not include any activities contrary to the following Executive Orders: Executive Order 14173: “Ending Illegal Discrimination and Restoring Merit-Based Opportunity Executive Order 14287: “Protecting American Communities from Criminal Aliens” Executive Order 14168: Defending Women from Gender Ideology Extremism and Restoring Biological Truth to the Federal Government Organizational Capacity and Record on Previous Grants – 20 points: The project proposal demonstrates that the organization has sufficient expertise, skills, and human resources to implement the project, including internal contr ols in place to manage federal funds. The organization demonstrates that it has a clear understanding of the underlying issue that the project will address. The organization demonstrates capacity for successful planning and responsible fiscal management. This includes a financial management system , a bank account , and if applicable, satisfactory audit findings. Applicants who have received grant funds previously have been compliant with applicable rules and regulations , including the Award Provisions and Standard Terms and Conditions. Where partners are described, the applicant details each partner’s respective role and provides curriculum vitae (CVs) for persons responsible for the project and financial administration. Proposed personnel, institutional resources, and partners are adequate and appropriate. Project Planning/Ability to Achieve Objectives – 25 points: The project plan is well developed, with sufficient detail about how activities will be carried out. The proposal specifies target audiences, participant recruitment, and geographic areas of implementation. The proposal outlines clear, achievable objectives. The proposal includes a reasonable implementation timeline. The project scope is appropriate and clearly defined. Budget – 15 points: The budget and narrative justification are sufficiently detailed. The budget demonstrates that the organization has devoted time to accurately determine expenses associated with the project instead of providing rough estimates. Costs are reasonable in relation to the proposed activities and anticipated results. The results and proposed outcomes justify the total cost of the project. Budget items are reasonable, allowable, and allocable. Monitoring and Evaluation – 10 points: There is a complete and thorough draft submission of a M&E Performance Monitoring Plan (PMP). This will include a list of proposed project activities, corresponding milestone, output, and outcome indicators, a description of data collection methods, and a timeline for collecting such information. The proposal presents a clear theory of change on how the program will address that problem. Funded projects will have their plans finalized during the negotiation phase, and monitoring plans may be subject to periodic updates throughout the life of the project. Sustainability – 10 points: The project proposal describes clearly the approach that will be used to ensure maximum sustainability or advancement of project goals after the end of project activity. 2. Indirect Costs If two or more applications receive equivalent scores based on the evaluation criteria outlined in this NOFO, preference will be given to the applicant with the lower indirect cost rate, as consistent with Executive Order 14332, Section 4(b)(iii). This preference will only be applied as a tie-breaking mechanism and does not supersede the primary evaluation criteria. 3. Review and Selection Process Acknowledgement of receipt. Applicants will receive acknowledgment of receipt of their proposal. Review. All submissions are screened for technical eligibility. If a submission is missing any required forms/documents listed above in Section D. Application Contents and Format , it will be considered ineligible and will not be reviewed by the grants review committee. A technical review panel will review eligible proposals based upon the criteria noted in this NOFO. Follow up notification. Applicants will generally be notified within 120 days after the NOFO deadline regarding the results of the review panel. 4.Risk Review i. Under the merit review as required by 2 CFR 200.206, prior to making a Federal Award the Department will review and consider the following risk factors: Financial stability Management systems and standards History of performance Audit reports and findings Ability to effectively implement project requirements ii. Responsibility/Qualification Information in SAM.gov Include the following language if the total Federal share of any award under this NOFO will be greater than the simplified acquisition threshold ($350,000): The Federal awarding agency, prior to making a Federal award with a total amount of Federal share greater than the simplified acquisition threshold, is required to review and consider any information about the applicant that is in the U.S. government designated integrity and performance system accessible through SAM.gov (see 41 U.S.C. 2313). An applicant can review and comment on any information in the responsibility/qualification records available in SAM.gov. Before making decisions in the risk review required by 2 CFR 200.206, the Department will consider any comments by the applicant, along with information available in the responsibility/qualification records in SAM.gov. iii. High Risk Designation Awardees that are deemed to be high risk based on the above risk factors will be held to special award conditions. At a minimum, the recipient and/or project designated as High Risk will be required to submit monthly narrative reports and/or quarterly detailed financial reports. Recipients may also be required, upon request of the Grants Officer or Grants Officer Representative, to provide electronic copies of receipts or other supporting documentation (e.g., timesheets, travel documents) for costs incurred. The Grants Officer may withhold 10% of the award amount until final reports have been reviewed and approved by the GO. The recipient may be required to pay all salaries supported by the grant via electronic funds transfer. Other special award conditions may also be included if deemed appropriate by the Grants Officer.   G. AWARD NOTICES The award or cooperative agreement will be written, signed, awarded, and administered by the Grants Officer. The award agreement is the authorizing document, and it will be provided to the recipient for review and counter-signature. The recipient may only start incurring project expenses beginning on the start date shown on the award document signed by the Grants Officer. If a proposal is selected for funding, the Department of State has no obligation to provide any additional future funding. Renewal of an award to increase funding or extend the period of performance is at the discretion of the Department of State. Issuance of this NOFO does not constitute an award commitment on the part of the U.S. government, nor does it commit the U.S. government to pay for costs incurred in the preparation and submission of proposals. Further, the U.S. government reserves the right to reject any or all proposals received. Payment Method: Recipients will be required to request payments by completing form SF-270—Request for Advance or Reimbursement and submitting the form to the Grants Officer and Grants Officer Representative. Recipients may not draw down funds without the affirmative authorization of the Department of State. In addition, recipients must submit, with each SF-270 payment request, a detailed explanation justifying the request. H. Post-Award Requirements and Administration 1. Administrative and National Policy Requirements Before submitting an application, applicants should review all the terms and conditions and required certifications which will apply to this award, to ensure that they will be able to comply. These include: In accordance with the Office of Management and Budget’s guidance located at 2 CFR part 200, all applicable Federal laws, and relevant Executive guidance, the Department of State will review and consider applications for funding, as applicable to specific programs, pursuant to this notice of funding opportunity in accordance with the following: Guidance for Grants and Agreements in Title 2 of the Code of Federal Regulations (2 CFR), as updated in the Federal Register’s 89 FR 30046 on April 22, 2024, particularly on: Selecting recipients most likely to be successful in delivering results based on the program objectives through an impartial process of evaluating Federal award applications (2 CFR part 200.205), Promoting the freedom of speech and religious liberty in alignment with Promoting Free Speech and Religious Liberty (E.O. 13798) and Improving Free Inquiry, Transparency, and Accountability at Colleges and Universities (E.O. 13864) (§§ 200.300, 200.303, 200.339, and 200.341), Providing a preference, to the extent permitted by law, to maximize use of goods, products, and materials produced in the United States (2 CFR part 200.322), and Terminating agreements pursuant to the U.S. Department of State Standard Terms and Conditions, including, to the greatest extent authorized by law, if an award no longer effectuates the program goals or agency priorities (2 CFR part 200.340). For the avoidance of doubt, the Department has sole discretion over the determination that an award no longer effectuates program goals or agency priorities, and this provision permits awards to be terminated at the Department’s convenience, including when it determines that the award no longer advances the national interest. 2 CFR 25 – UNIVERSAL IDENTIFIER AND SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT 2 CFR 170 – REPORTING SUBAWARD AND EXECUTIVE COMPENSATION INFORMATION 2 CFR 175 – AWARD TERM FOR TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS 2 CFR 182 – GOVERNMENTWIDE REQUIREMENTS FOR DRUG-FREE WORKPLACE (FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE) 2 CFR 183 – NEVER CONTRACT WITH THE ENEMY 2 CFR 600 – DEPARTMENT OF STATE REQUIREMENTS U.S. DEPARTMENT OF STATE STANDARD TERMS AND CONDITIONS Recipients must comply with all applicable Executive Orders. A searchable list can be found in the Federal Register: https://www.federalregister.gov/ . 2. Reporting Reporting Requirements: Recipients will be required to submit financial reports and program reports. The award document will specify what reports are required and how often these reports must be submitted. Note : most recipients will be required to submit quarterly program progress and financial reports throughout the project period. The quarterly progress report should include an up-to-date copy of the PMP datasheet. Progress and financial reports are due 30 days after the reporting period. Final certified programmatic and financial reports are due 120 days after the close of the project period. All reports are to be submitted electronically. The Awardee must also provide the AIT on an annual basis an inventory of all the U.S. government provided equipment using the SF428 form. Foreign Assistance Data Review: As required by Congress, the Department of State must make progress in its efforts to improve tracking and reporting of foreign assistance data through the Foreign Assistance Data Review (FADR). The FADR requires tracking of foreign assistance activity data from budgeting, planning, and allocation through obligation and disbursement. Successful applicants will be required to report and draw down federal funding based on the appropriate FADR Data Elements, indicated within their award documentation. In cases of more than one FADR Data Element, typically program or sector and/or regions or country, the successful applicant will be required to maintain separate accounting records. If the federal share of the award will include more than $500,000 over the period of performance, insert the following language: Applicants should be aware of the post award reporting requirements reflected in 2 CFR 200 Appendix XII—Award Term and Condition for Recipient Integrity and Performance Matters . 3.Branding and Marking The Department of State, its programs, and U.S. Government funding and assistance should be easily identifiable to the Department’s global audiences. Recipients of federal assistance awards must follow the branding guidance published at Guidance for Contracts and Grants – U.S. Department of State Brand System. Branding policy exceptions are outlined in the U.S. Department of State Foreign Affairs Manual 10 FAM 416, Policy Exceptions. For more information, visit: https://brand.america.gov/ I. Other Information Guidelines for Budget Justification Personnel and Fringe Benefits: Describe the wages, salaries, and benefits of temporary or permanent staff who will be working directly for the applicant on the program, and the percentage of their time that will be spent on the program. Travel: Estimate the costs of travel and per diem for this program, for program staff, consultants or speakers, and participants/beneficiaries. If the program involves international travel, include a brief statement of justification for that travel. Equipment: Describe any machinery, furniture, or other personal property that is required for the program, which has a useful life of more than one year (or a life longer than the duration of the program), and costs at least $10,000 per unit. Supplies: List and describe all the items and materials, including any computer devices, that are needed for the program. If an item costs more than $10,000 per unit, then put it in the budget under Equipment. Contractual: Describe goods and services that the applicant plans to acquire through a contract with a vendor. Also describe any sub-awards to non-profit partners that will help carry out the program activities. Other Direct Costs: Describe other costs directly associated with the program, which do not fit in the other categories. For example, shipping costs for materials and equipment or applicable taxes. All “Other” or “Miscellaneous” expenses must be itemized and explained. Indirect Costs: These are costs that cannot be linked directly to the program activities, such as overhead costs needed to help keep the organization operating. If your organization has a Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate (NICRA) and includes NICRA charges in the budget, attach a copy of your latest NICRA. Organizations that have never had a NICRA may request indirect costs of 15% of Modified Total Direct Costs (MTDC) as defined in 2 CFR 200.1. “Cost Sharing” refers to contributions from the organization or other entities other than AIT. It also includes in-kind contributions such as volunteers’ time and donated venues. Alcoholic Beverages: Please note that award funds cannot be used for alcoholic beverages and other entertainment related expenses. STEP Enrollment U.S. citizens who travel t o Taiwan are encouraged to enroll in the Department of State’s Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) available at: https://step.state.gov/step/ . Enrollment enables citizens to receive security-related messages from AIT and makes it easier for us to locate you in an emergency. AIT also recommends that all travelers review the State Department’s travel website at travel.state.gov for the Travel Warnings , Travel Alerts, and Taiwan Specific Information.   The post Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO): Implementation of 2027 GCTF Workshop in Eswatini appeared first on American Institute in Taiwan .

content:
USNI 新闻图 这些是根据海军和公开数据，截至 2026 年 11 月 9 日，美国海军在世界各地部署的航母打击群和两栖战备群的大致位置。如果 CSG 或 ARG 正在进行分类操作，图表会反映主力舰的位置。 2026 年 10 月 11 日，在日本，航空水手长的大副飞行员 Tykwon Young（右）和航空水手长的大副飞行员 Saabirah Parker 在停泊在佐世保湾的美国级两栖攻击舰的黎波里号 (LHA-7) 的飞行甲板上涂上小白眼。美国海军照片 USS 的黎波里号 (LHA-7) 停泊在日本佐世保港口。 2026 年 11 月 5 日，在日本海，第 13 海军陆战队远征队第 2/4 营登陆队的一名海军陆战队员在黄蜂级两栖攻击舰马金岛号 (LHD-8) 上进行静态快速绳索训练。美国海军陆战队照片 据舰艇观察员称，美国海军陆战队照片两栖攻击舰马金岛号 (LHD-8) 于周六从日本横须贺出发。马金岛两栖准备大队包括马金岛、安克雷奇号航空母舰 (LPD-23)、约翰·P·穆萨号航空母舰 (LPD-26) 和已上船的第 13 海军陆战队远征部队，目前正在日本海执行任务。 2026 年 10 月 22 日，来自新墨西哥州阿尔伯克基的加勒比海船体维护技术员二等迈克尔·布卢瓦斯三世 (Michael Bloise III) 在加勒比海航行的自由级濒海战斗舰明尼阿波利斯-圣保罗号 (LCS-21) 上进行焊接操作。
美国海军照片 濒海战斗舰明尼阿波利斯-圣保罗号 (LCS-21) 正在加勒比海中部作业。自由级濒海战斗舰驻扎在佛罗里达州梅波特海军基地。在地中海，三级内政通信电工 Micah Lee 在与刘易斯和克拉克级干货船 USNS Medgar Evers (T-AKE-13) 一起在阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰 USS 上进行海上补给之前检查通信设备巴尔克利号（DDG-84）在地中海，2026 年 10 月 22 日。美国海军照片 在地中海执行任务的独立部署的导弹驱逐舰包括：奥斯卡·奥斯汀号航空母舰（DDG-79），母港为罗塔海军基地。 USS Bulkeley (DDG-84)，母港为罗塔海军基地。美国海军保罗·伊格纳修斯号 (DDG-117)，母港为罗塔海军基地。斯托特号 (DDG-55) 母港位于弗吉尼亚州诺福克海军基地。2026 年 10 月 6 日，美国海军水手在阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰奥斯卡·奥斯汀号 (DDG-79) 上的驾驶室里站岗，当时该舰正通过苏伊士运河。美国海军照片 有两艘导弹驱逐舰在红海执行任务： USS Jason Dunham (DDG-109)，母港为佛罗里达州梅波特海军基地。美国海军冈萨雷斯号 (DDG-66)，母港为弗吉尼亚州诺福克海军基地。2026 年 11 月 7 日，在阿拉伯海，乔治·华盛顿号航空母舰 (CVN-73) 与刘易斯和克拉克级干货和弹药舰沃利·施艾拉号 (T-AKE-8) 一起进行海上补给。
美国海军照片 乔治华盛顿号航空母舰 (CVN-73) 以及第 5 号舰载航空联队 (CVW) 和舒普号航空母舰 (DDG-86) 正在阿拉伯海执行任务，以支持美国在中东的行动。 2026 年 10 月 30 日，隶属于第 147 攻击战斗机中队 (VFA) 的第 5 航母战斗群的一架 F-35C 闪电 II 准备从尼米兹级航空母舰乔治·华盛顿号航空母舰 (CVN-73) 的飞行甲板起飞。美国海军照片航空母舰乔治·华盛顿号 (CVN-73)，母港为日本横须贺。航母航空联队 5 “皇家狼牙棒”

内容摘要：中华人民共和国 (PRC) 正在扩大对 RISC-V（一种开源芯片设计标准）的使用，并扩大其对管理该标准的国际非营利组织的影响力。近年来，人们越来越担心被切断与 Arm 和英特尔等西方行业领导者设计的芯片的联系。中国公司现在不仅为消费设备而且为服务器和数据中心制造 RISC-V 芯片，尽管它们的功能不如专有芯片。 V100于10月推出，由国家支持的实体共同创建，号称是首款完全符合RISC-V服务器标准的通用芯片。国家级政策文件传统上避免直接讨论RISC-V，但今年9月，《电子信息制造业“十五五”规划》宣布，要求推进RISC-V研发和产业化，开发人工智能（AI）RISC-V芯片。 RISC-V 为自力更生带来了明显的好处，并且芯片可以进行调整，包括针对军事用例进行优化。
然而，中国的分析师担心芯片的“玻璃天花板”，甚至国家 IT 替代计划也指出，在政府系统中用于替代外国技术的 RISC-V 芯片的份额“可以忽略不计”。 10月19日，深圳芯片制造商进迭时空与香山处理器团队在第六届RISC-V中国峰会上推出了新型46核服务器芯片V100。[1]其制造商宣称其是首款完全符合RISC-V服务器标准的通用芯片（21世纪经济报道，10月19日；科技日报，10月20日）。 RISC-V 是一种开源指令集架构 (ISA)，是处理器运行的语言。与全球几乎所有计算机和手机中使用的 Arm 或 Intel x86 等专有 ISA 不同，任何人都可以使用 RISC-V，无需支付许可费或需要其他权限。由英国和美国公司制造的 Arm 和英特尔处理器必须遵守这些国家政府实施的许可和出口管制。相比之下，RISC-V 主要由 RISC-V International 监管，这是一家总部位于瑞士的非营利组织，旨在避免此类漏洞。最近推出的服务器芯片代表了中华人民共和国（PRC）该行业更广泛的趋势。
北京最初在 2010 年代中期开始将 RISC-V 视为对抗西方技术霸权并扩大其在新兴技术领域结构性力量的一种方式（中国简报，2023 年 12 月 15 日）。此后，北京通过国家主导的政策支持鼓励其发展，从城市层面开始，逐步上升到国家层面。尽管这些芯片的功能仍然落后于西方竞争对手，但它们越来越多地部署在数据中心的服务器中，而不仅仅是嵌入消费设备中。从市政厅到五年计划 2023年以来，地方层面对RISC-V的支持已经明确，特别是在上海、北京和深圳等一线城市（中国简报，2023年12月15日）。北京经济技术开发区的目标是到 2030 年使 RISC-V 产业价值超过 500 亿元人民币（70 亿美元），据一些估计，届时全国市场将达到约 2200 亿元人民币（210 亿美元）（北京市政府，2025 年 1 月 3 日；中国日报）

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary: The People’s Republic of China (PRC) is expanding its use of RISC-V, an open-source chip design standard, as well as its influence over the international nonprofit organization that manages it. This follows growing fears in recent years of being cut off from chips designed by Western industry leaders such as Arm and Intel. PRC firms are now creating RISC-V chips not just for consumer devices but for servers and data centers, even though they are less powerful than proprietary chips. The V100, launched in October and co-created by a state-backed entity, is billed as the first general-purpose chip fully compliant with RISC-V server standards. National-level policy documents have traditionally avoided discussing RISC-V directly, but in September, the 15th Five-Year Plan for the Electronic Information Manufacturing Industry announced calls to advance RISC-V research, development, and industrialization, and to develop RISC-V chips for artificial intelligence (AI). RISC-V brings clear benefits for self-reliance, and the chips can be adapted, including being optimized for military use cases. Analysts in the PRC worry, however, about a “glass ceiling” for the chips, and even the state IT substitution program has noted that the share of RISC-V chips it has used to replace foreign technology in government systems is “negligible.” On October 19, Shenzhen-based chipmaker SpacemiT (进迭时空) and the state-backed XiangShan (香山) processor team launched the V100, a new 46-core server chip, at the sixth RISC-V Summit China.  [1] Its makers bill it as the first general-purpose chip fully compliant with RISC-V server standards ( 21st Century Business Herald , October 19; Science and Technology Daily , October 20). RISC-V is an open-source instruction set architecture (ISA), which is the language that processors run on. Unlike proprietary ISAs, such as Arm or Intel’s x86 that are used in almost all of the world’s computers and phones, anyone can use RISC-V without paying a license fee or requiring other permissions. Arm and Intel processors, made by British and U.S. companies, must abide by licensing and export controls put in place by those countries’ governments. By comparison, RISC-V is mainly overseen by RISC-V International, a Switzerland-based nonprofit that avoids such vulnerabilities. The recently unveiled server chip is representative of broader trends in the sector within the People’s Republic of China (PRC). Beijing initially began to view RISC-V as a way to counter the West’s technological hegemony and extend its structural power in emerging technologies in the mid-2010s ( China Brief , December 15, 2023). Since then, it has encouraged its development through state-led policy support, starting at the city level and moving up to the national level. Although the chips’ capabilities remain behind those of Western rivals, they are increasingly being deployed in servers for data centers, not just embedded in consumer devices. From City Halls to the Five-Year Plan Since 2023, local-level support for RISC-V has been explicit, especially in first-tier cities like Shanghai, Beijing, and Shenzhen ( China Brief , December 15, 2023). Beijing’s Economic-Technological Development Area aims for a RISC-V industry worth more than renminbi (RMB) 50 billion ($7 billion) by 2030, at which point the national market will reach around RMB 220 billion ($21 billion), according to some estimates ( Beijing Municipal Government , January 3, 2025; China Daily , October 22). National-level documents have tended instead to use the term “open source” to implicitly refer to RISC-V. In mid-September, however, the 15th Five-Year Plan for the Electronic Information Manufacturing Industry announced calls to “advance the research, development, and industrialization of RISC-V” (推进第五代精简指令集 (RISC-V) 研发与产业化), and to support RISC-V artificial intelligence (AI) and embedded system chips ( Ministry of Information and Industry Technology , September 15).  [2] Server Ambitions, Smartphone-Class Silicon RISC-V’s strength so far has been in cheaper control chips for appliances and cars, but newer chips signal data center servers as an emerging use case. The Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) calls the open-source XiangShan core the most powerful of its kind in the world ( China Daily , March 26). Beyond the latest processor from SpacemiT and XiangShan, Alibaba now offers a server-class design, the C950, that it says performs on par with Apple’s M1 chip, which it released in 2020, on a standard performance test ( The Register , March 25). Engineers usually judge how well a core is designed via a two-step process. First, they run an industry-standard test, which times how long a processor takes to complete a set of tasks, and turns that time into a score. Second, they divide the score by the core’s clock speed, which is the number of steps it takes each second, measured in gigahertz (GHz). The result measures how much work a core does in each step (see Figure 1). On this metric, PRC progress is substantial: XiangShan’s cores have roughly doubled since 2021. however, comes from a computer simulation—they are yet to run the tests on physical chips. In an independent test run on SpacemiT’s most recently commercially produced desktop and edge chip showed it as running slightly slower than the U.K.-designed Raspberry Pi 5 hobby computer, which was released in 2023 ( CNX Software , January 23). The speed that a core runs matters too, as a chip with a well-designed core may still lose out in the long term to a more basic chip whose core has a faster clock speed. Measured at the speeds they actually run, the best cores in the SpacemiT/XiangShan processor are well behind Nvidia’s leading Grace server processor, and those produced by Arm and Intel (see Figure 2). Alibaba’s C950, which it licenses to other chipmakers, comes close to or beats Grace based on the firm’s internal testing.
