summary: 总部位于新加坡的科技集团 Megaspeed 经营着价值数十亿美元的世界上最先进的人工智能芯片，但法新社访问时，其办公室已是空壳，其员工似乎早在间谍指控传到他们家门口之前就消失了。数据中心公司 MegaSpeed International 的新加坡办事处。照片：Taryn/法新社 Megaspeed 前董事 Alice Huang 本周被指控为中国间谍，被指控在为北京挖掘公司机密时与 Nvidia 联合创始人 Jensen Huang 有染。爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 的生活细节模糊不清，几乎令人印象深刻
content:
总部位于新加坡的科技集团 Megaspeed 经营着价值数十亿美元的世界上最先进的人工智能芯片，但法新社访问时，其办公室已是空壳，其员工似乎早在间谍指控传到他们家门口之前就消失了。数据中心公司 MegaSpeed International 的新加坡办事处。照片：Taryn/法新社 Megaspeed 前董事 Alice Huang 本周被指控为中国间谍，被指控在为北京挖掘公司机密时与 Nvidia 联合创始人 Jensen Huang 有染。关于爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 的生活细节很模糊，几乎不可能确定她住在哪里、在哪里工作、或者出生时间。但她的影响力无疑是广泛传播的，从不起眼的新加坡办公室，到东南亚庞大的数据中心，再到硅谷闪闪发光的董事会会议室。她与云计算公司 Megaspeed 的关系是丑闻的核心。 Megaspeed 标榜自己是一家处于人工智能革命核心的公司，使用 Nvidia 的先进硅芯片为大型数据中心内的高性能计算提供动力。但它也因一个更隐秘的目的而受到调查。据称，Megaspeed 打着为其东南亚数据中心购买计算机硬件的幌子，通过向中国运送 Nvidia 芯片来帮助北京规避贸易限制。北京方面否认了间谍活动的指控，Megaspeed 表示正在调查其是否遵守了敏感芯片的出口管制。
在位于新加坡商业区中心的 Megaspeed 办公室，锁着的玻璃门后面看不到任何工作人员。邻居告诉法新社，过去几个月他们没有看到任何人进出。同样，在距离新加坡仅一桥之隔的马来西亚柔佛州新开发社区的一家购物中心里，子公司 Speedmatrix 的办公室里也没有员工。 2025 年 5 月 22 日，数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的中国高管 Alice Huang（右）出席 Nvidia 首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋（左）在台北一家餐厅举办的晚宴。照片：法新社照片 / CTI via AFPTV。新加坡警方于 2025 年 2 月对 Megaspeed 和其他几家涉嫌规避或违反出口管制的公司展开调查。作为新加坡调查的一部分，爱丽丝·黄接受了采访。新加坡内政部表示，尽管没有受到任何指控，但她于 2026 年 2 月被禁止进入新加坡，原因是提供不准确信息以“淡化她在 Megaspeed 中的作用”。爆炸性增长 公司记录显示黄直接参与了 Megaspeed 的诞生。记录显示，与她有联系的一家公司于 2023 年初收购了中国视频游戏开发商第七大道国际的新加坡子公司。几乎立刻，7Road 的名称就被抛弃并改为 Megaspeed International。黄在 2023 年 3 月至 2023 年 11 月期间担任 Megaspeed 董事不到一年。
她的到来恰逢命运的巨大变化，Megaspeed 从一家名不见经传的视频游戏制造商转变为亚洲最大的 Nvidia 芯片买家之一。根据 2024 年提交的公司账目，在 12 个月内，Megaspeed 的收入从 0 美元跃升至近 3 亿美元。Megaspeed 自称为“云托管服务提供商”，其资产价值从 3200 万美元飙升至近 30 亿美元。期间。 Nvidia 的 H200 芯片。照片：英伟达。只是哦

【原文 English Original】
Singapore-based tech group Megaspeed dealt in billions of dollars’ worth of the world’s most advanced AI chips, but its office was an empty shell when AFP visited, its staff seemingly vanished long before claims of espionage landed at their door. The Singapore office of the data centre company MegaSpeed International. Photo: Taryn/AFP Megaspeed’s former director Alice Huang was this week outed as an alleged Chinese spy, accused of having an affair with Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang while digging up company secrets for Beijing. Details about Alice Huang’s life are vague, making it almost impossible to pin down where she lives, where she works, or when she was born. But her influence undoubtedly spreads far and wide, from the nondescript Singapore office, to hulking data centres in Southeast Asia, to the gleaming boardrooms of Silicon Valley. Her connection to cloud computing firm Megaspeed sits at the centre of the scandal. Megaspeed touts itself as a company at the heart of the AI revolution, using Nvidia’s advanced silicon chips to power high-performance computing inside vast data centres. But it is also under investigation for serving a murkier purpose. Under the guise of buying computer hardware for its Southeast Asia data hubs, Megaspeed has allegedly helped Beijing skirt trade restrictions by sending Nvidia chips into China. Beijing has denied allegations of spying, and Megaspeed said it was investigating if it had complied with export controls on the sensitive chips. At Megaspeed’s office in the heart of the Singapore business district, no staff could be seen behind its locked glass doors. Neighbours told AFP they had not seen anyone come or go for the past few months. Likewise in a mall at a newly developed neighbourhood in Johor, the Malaysian region a bridge away from Singapore, no employees were around in subsidiary Speedmatrix’s office. Alice Huang (R), a Chinese executive linked to the data centre company called Megaspeed, attending a dinner hosted by Nvidia’s chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang (L in black back facing camera) at a restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025. Photo: AFP photo/ CTI via AFPTV. Singapore police opened an investigation in February 2025 into Megaspeed and several other companies suspected of circumventing or violating export controls. Alice Huang was interviewed as part of Singapore’s probe. Although no charges were laid, she was barred from the city-state in February 2026 for providing inaccurate information to “downplay her role in Megaspeed”, Singapore’s home ministry said. Explosive growth Corporate records show Huang’s direct involvement in the birth of Megaspeed. A company linked to her acquired the Singapore arm of Chinese video game developer 7Road International in early 2023, the records showed. Almost immediately, the 7Road name was ditched and changed to Megaspeed International. Huang was listed as a Megaspeed director for less than a year, taking the role between March and November 2023. Her arrival coincided with a drastic change in fortunes, as Megaspeed pivoted from a little-known video game maker to one of Asia’s biggest buyers of Nvidia chips. Within 12 months, Megaspeed’s revenue jumped from $0 to almost US$300 million, according to company accounts filed in 2024. Megaspeed — which described itself as a “cloud hosting services provider” — saw the value of its assets skyrocket from $32 million to almost $3 billion over the same period. Nvidia’s H200 chips. Photo: Nvidia. Just one of Nvidia’s advanced AI computer chips can cost tens of thousands of dollars. Over two years, Megaspeed reportedly traded in upwards of $4 billion worth of Nvidia chips. A financial trail weaving through Singapore, Malaysia and the Cayman Islands suggests Megaspeed’s business may have been boosted by a connection to Chinese tech giant Alibaba. Megaspeed has a Malaysian subsidiary that struck a deal in 2024 pledging assets to Apex Enterprise Solutions in Singapore as security in case of contractual breaches. Apex is linked through a parent company to Alibaba Group Holding Ltd, a firm registered in the Cayman Islands, Singapore corporate data shows. By that time, Huang was no longer registered as a director at Megaspeed. But Singapore authorities said she remained one of Megaspeed’s “key controllers”. Megaspeed’s ultimate holding company is a Singapore firm called Swiftdata. Singapore businessman Tan Yong Pong — who has previously run printing and graphic design companies — is a director of both Megaspeed and Swiftdata. No one answered when AFP visited Tan’s registered address in eastern Singapore, although dogs could be heard barking behind the door. “They are friendly. I occasionally bump into the lady at the lift landing when she’s walking her dog,” an elderly neighbour told AFP. “But we have not seen them for months.” Awkward questions In June 2025, US investigators turned up at Megaspeed to carry out a “post-shipment verification”, with Huang present, according to Singapore’s home ministry, adding that it was the first time it found out about Washington’s probe. The American flag is raised on the newly-installed flagpole on the South Lawn of the White House on June 18, 2025. Photo: White House, via Flickr. That same day, Huang was interviewed by Singapore police who impounded her passport. By then, she and Nvidia boss Jensen Huang had already been spotted together in public. In one of their early outings together, they were seen mingling at an afterparty following the Computex trade show in Taiwan at the beginning of 2024. Trump was briefed on the intelligence findings about their relationship well before it exploded into a public scandal, but said Sunday he did not regret not acting on it. “No, I don’t think so. I think — you know, he’s an honorable guy,” Trump said. But the scandal has sparked national security fears. China and the United States are fighting for supremacy in artificial intelligence, and Nvidia’s market-leading products have become a major point of contention. Nvidia controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for the chips used to train and run AI models, and the US imposed rules in 2022 to restrict their sales to China. In the past years, Jensen Huang has emerged as the leading tech boss urging  Trump to lift those curbs. In any case, the restrictions appear to have been widely circumvented. Singapore. File photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. A Chinese university tied to the nation’s defence establishment was able to buy advanced Nvidia chips, according to procurement notices from October and September. Singapore’s probe into Megaspeed is ongoing. Separately, Malaysia said Friday it is investigating the company’s subsidiary Speedmatrix to determine if chips imported into the country had been exported to other jurisdictions. Megaspeed itself said it has retained a US lawfirm to examine its compliance. “Megaspeed takes its compliance obligations under US export control laws extremely seriously,” it said. Tangled webs Alice Huang sits in the middle of a corporate web, connected to myriad shell companies, investment houses and major Chinese technology firms. Corporate records filed in Hong Kong list her as a director of Nanjing Lingxing Technology, which operates the popular T3 ride hailing platform in China. Other notable investors in Nanjing Lingxing Technology include Alibaba and Tencent, as well as state-backed carmakers like China FAW and Dongfeng Motor Group. A corporate CV published by a Chinese investment firm details Huang’s rapid ascent through the ranks of Asian investment banking. She served in a senior role at HSBC sometime around 2012, the resume claims, before moving on to stints at CITIC Securities and Shanghai Hexi Investment. The HSBC headquarters in Central, Hong Kong. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Singapore business filings described her as a Chinese citizen with a Hong Kong passport. She was born in China’s landlocked Hunan province, which she left to study media in Hong Kong, HK01 media reported. A CCTV reporter wrote on Weibo that she worked with Huang at the Chinese broadcaster, but later deleted the post.

title: Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China: White House
zh_title: 特朗普、习近平、普京将在中国举行历史性会晤：白宫
summary: 白宫周五表示，唐纳德·特朗普、弗拉基米尔·普京和习近平将于下周在深圳举行的峰会上举行美国、俄罗斯和中国领导人之间的首次三方会晤。 2026 年 7 月 6 日星期一，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在椭圆形办公室举行的特朗普账户启动活动中敲响了纽约证券交易所和纳斯达克的开盘钟。照片：Joyce N. Boghosian，来自 Flickr。特朗普希望在周四的三边会谈中讨论削减核武库的问题，并且还将提及他在伊朗的战争，但预计他不会讨论俄罗斯
content:
白宫周五表示，唐纳德·特朗普、弗拉基米尔·普京和习近平将于下周在深圳举行的峰会上举行美国、俄罗斯和中国领导人之间的首次三方会晤。 2026 年 7 月 6 日星期一，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在椭圆形办公室举行的特朗普账户启动活动中敲响了纽约证券交易所和纳斯达克的开盘钟。照片：Joyce N. Boghosian，来自 Flickr。美国官员表示，特朗普希望在周四的三边会谈中讨论削减核武库的问题，并且还将提及他在伊朗的战争，但预计他不会讨论俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争。白宫发言人奥利维亚·威尔士告诉记者，三位领导人将在中国南方城市亚太经合组织峰会期间会面。 “总统已明确表示，除其他议题外，他将讨论世界范围内核武器的削减。特朗普总统认为，这种扩散非常危险，”威尔士说。美国官员表示，主导特朗普第二个总统任期的主要冲突之一将成为焦点，但另一个则不会。一位不愿透露姓名的美国高级官员在电话中对记者表示：“我认为总统确实打算在与习近平和普京的三边会议上讨论伊朗问题。” 2026 年 5 月 20 日，中国国家主席习近平在北京人民大会堂。照片：克里姆林宫。
这位官员补充说，华盛顿与基辅和莫斯科有“完全不同的轨道”谈判，旨在结束乌克兰战争。他指的是美国特使最近几天与普京和乌克兰总统泽连斯基进行的会谈。“中国实际上并不是该轨道的一部分，因此在那里讨论乌克兰问题似乎并不合适，”该官员补充道。官员们表示，特斯拉和 Space X 的老板埃隆·马斯克将陪同特朗普访华，但不会参与与习近平和普京的会面。特朗普周四还将与中国国家主席举行双边工作午餐和会晤，这是自美国总统去年重新掌权以来的第四次会面。但特朗普没有计划与普京进行单独的一对一会谈。官员们表示，除其他话题外，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋因与一名所谓的中国间谍有染而辞职的问题预计不会出现在特朗普与习近平的会晤中。 2026 年 5 月 20 日，中国国家主席习近平（左）在北京人民大会堂欢迎俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京。照片：克里姆林宫。另一位美国高级官员表示：“英伟达的情况实际上不会对此次访问产生任何影响。”美国也不打算讨论敏感芯片技术的出口管制，而这正是英伟达丑闻的核心。 “我们不就美国的出口管制进行谈判。
第二位官员表示：“这些都是我们在政府中制定的国家安全问题……我们不希望它出现在我们在那里与中国人的任何对话中。”特朗普将于周一离开华盛顿，周二抵达菲律宾参加东南亚国家联盟（ASEAN）峰会，然后前往深圳。

【原文 English Original】
Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week, the White House said Friday. US President Donald Trump rings the opening bell for the New York Stock Exchange and the Nasdaq during an event to launch Trump Accounts, Monday, July 6, 2026, in the Oval Office. Photo: Joyce N. Boghosian, via Flickr. Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals at the trilateral talks on Thursday and is also set to bring up his war in Iran — but he is not expected to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine, US officials said. The three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters. “The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous,” Wales said. One of the major conflicts dominating Trump’s second term as president will feature, but the other will not, the US officials said. “I think the president does intend to talk about Iran in the trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin,” a senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters on a call. Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on May 20, 2026. Photo: The Kremlin. Washington has a “whole other track” of negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, the official added, referring to talks that US envoys have had in recent days with Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. “China is not really a part of that track, so it doesn’t seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there,” the official added. Tesla and Space X boss Elon Musk will accompany Trump on his trip to China but won’t be involved in the meeting with Xi and Putin, the officials said. Trump will also hold a bilateral working lunch and meeting with the Chinese president on Thursday — their fourth meeting since the US president’s return to power last year. But Trump is not scheduled to have a separate one-on-one with Putin. Among other topics, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s resignation over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy is not expected to come up in Trump’s meetings with Xi, the officials said. Chinese President Xi Jinping (left) welcomes Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on May 20, 2026. Photo: The Kremlin. “The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip,” a second US senior official said. The United States also did not plan to discuss export controls on sensitive chip technology, which were at the heart of the Nvidia scandal. “We do not negotiate American export controls. These are national security matters that we develop in the administration… and we don’t expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we’re there,” the second official said. Trump will leave Washington on Monday and arrive in the Philippines on Tuesday for a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit before heading to Shenzhen.

title: Hong Kong receives 16 expressions of interest for Northern Metropolis logistics cluster
zh_title: 香港收到16份发展北都物流集群的意向书
summary: 政府表示，香港北部都会洪水桥/厦村发展区规划中的物流集群已收到 16 份意向书。这张航拍照片显示的是2026年10月30日，即将建成的洪水桥地铁站附近的益园村正在被拆除。照片的右上角显示了洪水桥大学城校园区规划的大片区域。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。当局周五宣布，这 16 份意见书来自开发商、物流运营商、行业协会和专业服务机构。
content:
政府表示，香港北部都会洪水桥/厦村发展区规划中的物流集群已收到 16 份意向书。这张航拍照片显示的是2026年10月30日，即将建成的洪水桥地铁站附近的益园村正在被拆除。照片的右上角显示了洪水桥大学城校园区规划的大片区域。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。当局周五宣布，这 16 份意见书来自开发商、物流运营商、行业协会和专业服务提供商，但没有透露具体姓名。他们表示对洪水桥/厦村新发展区一块约32公顷的土地感兴趣，当局已预留该土地用于在北方大都市西部建设“现代物流集群”。运输及物流局和土木工程拓展署负责监管这部分工程。 TLB 发言人表示，当局将开始分析提交的材料，以促进正式招标的规划和准备。该发言人补充道：“我们预计最早将于 2027 年底对第一批可用场地进行招标，并争取在 2028 年授予相关招标。”
政府表示，洪水桥/厦村物流集群将靠近深圳湾口岸，并连接香港国际机场和葵青货柜码头。立法会周四通过专门立法，简化监管程序并加快北部都会区的发展，该计划将把靠近深圳边境的香港约三分之一的土地转变为创新和科技中心。另请参阅：科技城到大学城：香港北部大都市为何将重点从高科技转向高等教育 当局表示，该大型项目的重点将是三个大学城，而之前提出的开发名为新田科技城的科技中心的要求则有所不同。

【原文 English Original】
A planned logistics cluster in the Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen development area in Hong Kong’s Northern Metropolis has received 16 expression-of-interest submissions, the government has said. This aerial photo shows the demolition of Yik Yuen Tsuen, a village near the future Hung Shui Kiu MTR station, October 30, 2026. On the top right corner of the photo shows a large area planned for the campus area of the Hung Shui Kiu University Town. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Authorities announced on Friday that the 16 submissions came from developers, logistics operators, industry associations and professional services providers, without naming them. They were signalling interest in a roughly 32-hectare land plot in the Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen New Development Area that authorities have reserved for building a “modern logistics cluster” in the western part of the Northern Metropolis. The Transport and Logistics Bureau (TLB) and the Civil Engineering and Development Department oversee this part of the project. A TLB spokesperson said authorities would start analysing the submissions to facilitate planning and the preparation of a formal tender. “We expect to invite tenders for the first available site(s) in end [of] 2027 at the earliest, with a view to awarding the relevant tender in 2028,” the spokesperson added. The Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen logistics cluster will be close to the Shenzhen Bay Port and connected to the Hong Kong International Airport and the Kwai Tsing Container Terminals, the government has said. Lawmakers on Thursday passed dedicated legislation that will streamline regulatory procedures and expedite the Northern Metropolis development, which is set to transform about a third of Hong Kong’s land area near its border with Shenzhen into an innovation and tech hub. See also: Technopole to University Towns: Why Hong Kong’s Northern Metropolis shifted focus from hi-tech to higher ed Authorities have said that the focus of the megaproject will be three university towns – shifting from the previously stated imperative of developing a tech hub known as the San Tin Technopole.

title: China’s Intelligence Coup in the AI War
zh_title: 人工智能战争中中国的情报政变
summary: ​​​​​​​本篇文章更新于下午4点35分。 2026 年 11 月 14 日。黄仁勋是间谍梦寐以求的目标。情报机构多年来一直在努力寻找一个能够如此接近如此有权有势的人的线人。这位英伟达前首席执行官也是唐纳德·特朗普的朋友，这让他变得更有价值。从一个角度来看，黄的行动非常简单：一位西方官员有点钦佩地告诉我，它展示了人类情报收集的力量和男性自我的弱点。关于中国国家安全部如何实施这一举措，目前仍有很多未知数。
content:
​​​​​​​本篇文章更新于下午4点35分。 2026 年 11 月 14 日。黄仁勋是间谍梦寐以求的目标。情报机构多年来一直在努力寻找一个能够如此接近如此有权有势的人的线人。这位英伟达前首席执行官也是唐纳德·特朗普的朋友，这让他变得更有价值。从一个角度来看，黄的行动非常简单：一位西方官员有点钦佩地告诉我，它展示了人类情报收集的力量和男性自我的弱点。关于中国国家安全部如何招募与科技巨头有婚外情的黄爱丽（无亲属关系），或者她可能提供了哪些信息，目前仍不得而知。中国官员驳斥了美国关于她是国家安全部人员的指控，认为这是毫无根据的诽谤，美国官员也没有提供他们认为表明她隶属关系的证据。但研究中国情报策略的专家告诉我，她可能不是一个训练有素、打算诱骗英伟达老板的特工。他们说，更有可能的是，国家安全部得知她与黄有染，然后招募了她。根据中国国家情报法，公民必须在国家安全部要求时提供协助。而且该机构并不总是善意地提出要求。前官员告诉我，国家安全局官员会通过威胁没收他们的财产或骚扰他们的家人来胁迫潜在资产。
四十多年来，中国在网络空间、外太空和实体领域无情地窃取美国机密。中国的黑客往往最受关注，因为他们渗透了无数的计算机网络，窃取了商业和官方机密，并为在与美国发生战争时可能瘫痪通信系统奠定了基础。但中国的间谍头子也建立了一个广泛的人脉网络，招募企业高管、大学教授、学生，甚至后来成为加州市长的一名教育家。 “中国正在将技术和创新作为发展经济和加强国家安全的国家战略的一部分，”中央情报局前副局长戴维·科恩告诉我。北京在应对与美国的竞争时高度关注人工智能，这导致美国军事规划者对潜在战争的爆发发出警告。中国国家主席习近平呼吁在人工智能和量子计算和生物技术等其他领域“爆发原创性和颠覆性创新”。如果案件官员要列出一份对人工智能发展及其管理规则影响最大的人名单，黄仁勋将位居榜首——至少在本周之前是这样。 “他不是一个令人惊讶的目标，”中央情报局前中国问题分析师康纳·福尔曼告诉我。 “他对公司和美国的政策目标、需求和目标有着深刻的洞察力。
他对一个民族国家具有超越筹码的巨大价值。”福尔曼说，国安部可能一直在寻找任何可以进入黄的世界的途径。黄爱丽丝“可能是在正确的时间、正确的地点出现的正确的人”，以提供国安部想要的访问权限。 “我对此一点也不感到惊讶。这就是中国所做的，”联邦调查局前反情报负责人艾伦·科勒告诉我。“有人在这里打出了全垒打，因为目标是黄仁勋。但中国也可能针对数十名从未听说过的 Nv 低级工程师

【原文 English Original】
​ ​​​​​​This story was updated at 4:35 p.m. on November 14, 2026. J ensen Huang is the kind of target that spies dream about. Intelligence agencies work for years to develop a source who can get so close to such a powerful man. That the former Nvidia CEO is also friends with Donald Trump makes him even more valuable. Viewed one way, the Huang operation is painfully simple: It demonstrated the power of human-intelligence gathering and the weakness of the male ego, one Western official told me, somewhat admiringly. Much remains unknown about how China’s Ministry of State Security might have enlisted Alice Huang (no relation), who was having an extramarital affair with the tech titan, or what information she might have provided. Chinese officials have dismissed the U.S. allegations that she is an MSS asset as baseless smears, and U.S. officials have not presented the evidence they believe shows her affiliation. But experts on China’s intelligence tactics told me that she was probably not a trained operative who set out to entrap the Nvidia boss. More likely, they said, the MSS learned she was having an affair with Huang and then recruited her. Under China’s National Intelligence Law, citizens are required to assist the MSS when asked. And the agency doesn’t always ask nicely. MSS officers are known to coerce potential assets by threatening to seize their property or harassing their family members, former officials told me. For more than four decades, China has relentlessly stolen U.S. secrets—in cyberspace, outer space, and in the flesh. China’s hackers tend to get the most attention because they have penetrated countless computer networks, vacuuming up commercial and official secrets and laying the groundwork to potentially cripple communications systems in the event of a war with the United States. But China’s spymasters have also created an extensive human network, recruiting business executives, university professors, students, and even an educator in California who later became mayor. “China is going after technology and innovation as part of a national strategy to develop their economy and strengthen their national security,” David Cohen, the former deputy director of the CIA, told me. Beijing is acutely focused on AI as it navigates its rivalry with the U.S., one that has led American military planners to warn about the outbreak of a potential war. China’s president, Xi Jinping, has called for “an explosion of original and disruptive innovations” in AI and other fields, including quantum computing and biotech. If a case officer were to make a list of who has the most influence over the development of AI and the rules governing it, Huang would have been at the top—at least until this week. “He’s not a surprising target,” Connor Forman, a former China analyst at the CIA, told me. “He has insight into the company and U.S. policy aims, needs, and goals. He’s of tremendous value to a nation-state, beyond chips.” The MSS would presumably have been looking for any avenue it could find into Huang’s world. Alice Huang “may have just been the right person in the right place at the right time” to provide the access that the MSS wanted, Forman said. “I’m not at all surprised by it. This is what China does,” Alan Kohler, the former head of counterintelligence for the FBI, told me. “Someone hit a home run here, because the target was Jensen Huang. But China is also likely targeting dozens of low-level engineers that no one has ever heard of at Nvidia and other tech companies.” A lice Huang was reportedly running a company called Megaspeed that rented computer processing power to companies in China. Chinese authorities could conceivably have threatened her business or, conversely, have offered to help her if she assisted them by spying on Jensen Huang and people in his orbit. U.S. and Chinese intelligence agencies wield very different tools. CIA officers don’t threaten Americans into cooperating or use honey traps—despite what paperback spy thrillers and Hollywood blockbusters might portray. Chinese espionage in the United States is pervasive, current and former officials told me. But ex-CIA officers also described their tradecraft as “horrible” and “clumsy,” particularly in cyber operations. After Xi became president in 2013, he reoriented Chinese intelligence to serve the country’s long-term strategic goals and put a stop to espionage by members of the military for their personal gain, according to a report by the Center for Strategic and International Studies. The think tank conducted a survey of publicly reported spying incidents from 2000 to 2023 and found that intelligence activity has increased significantly in the years after Xi came to power. Computer hacking was “China’s preferred mode” of clandestinely gathering information. [ Read: Will Taiwan just give up? ] In 2015, the scale of China’s cyberspying on U.S. companies became so intolerable that Barack Obama and Xi agreed that their countries would refrain from spying on each other’s companies for commercial advantage. It was a one-sided deal, because the United States already had an official prohibition against economic espionage—stealing foreign corporate secrets for the benefit of American companies. Only a year later, though, China was back to its rampant computer hacking, current and former officials have told me. But China hasn’t limited itself to hacking; it also uses traditional methods such as recruiting agents. The country’s intelligence apparatus often blurs the line between civilian and military worlds. Nearly half of all incidents that CSIS examined involved Chinese military or government employees. But 41 percent involved private citizens. “China uses what they call ‘nontraditional collectors,’” such as students and businesspeople, Anna Puglisi, a former U.S. national counterintelligence officer for East Asia, told me. “They view their diaspora worldwide as potential resources.” Only about 10 percent of the operations tracked by CSIS involved non-Chinese actors, usually U.S. persons recruited by Chinese officials. By contrast, the CIA works overseas to recruit foreigners to spy on its behalf. C hina and the United States are in an all-out AI race, and the Huang affair may be an example of the no-holds-barred approach the country takes to accessing AI chips and technology from the U.S. But winning doesn’t necessarily mean that China will be the first nation to develop artificial superintelligence or the most sophisticated models. “It means that China incorporates this technology better and more effectively than the U.S. can,” Forman, the former CIA analyst, told me. For example, AI could help China’s military make decisions faster on the battlefield, which has historically been a weak spot compared with the United States, Forman said. [ Read: NATO’s nightmare ] To build better AI systems, China needs the best chips. “Chinese AI chip capability still lags behind the United States,” Harry Krejsa, the director of studies at the Carnegie Mellon Institute for Strategy and Technology, told me. Eventually, China would like to produce its own cutting-edge chips, but in the meantime, he said, it has to obtain that technology through other means, including espionage or smuggling. Krejsa, who worked on technology and security issues at the White House and in the Pentagon, said he views the Jensen Huang incident as further evidence of how hard China is working to gain advantage. “I caution against seeing this as some game of 3-D chess, as opposed to a world-class intelligence service being opportunistic any chance it gets,” he said. “Any intelligence organization worth its salt is trying to get close to people” like Huang. Alice Huang may have helped China in other ways. At the same time U.S. officials suspect she was working with the MSS, Megaspeed, the Singapore-based company where Huang was an executive, had been under investigation by the Commerce Department for suspicion of shipping Nvidia chips to China in violation of U.S. export rules, former officials told me. Officials who run those kinds of investigations have regular access to relevant reporting from the intelligence community, but it’s not clear whether they knew about Huang’s suspected MSS affiliation. [ Read: Would Claude refuse an illegal military order? ] Trump reportedly was warned twice—the first time in 2025—that the U.S. believed Jensen Huang was having an affair with a suspected MSS asset, but he gave no instructions to notify the Nvidia chief and took no obvious actions to disrupt China’s spying. The New York Times reported last month that Huang was the suspected target of China’s spies. “If the U.S. government knew about this relationship for over a year, that sounds very long to let this play out without an intervention of some sort,” said Kohler, the former FBI counterintelligence chief, who now runs Pamir Consulting, which advises U.S. companies on Chinese influence. Former officials told me it was possible that the U.S. intelligence community wanted to continue monitoring Alice Huang, her company, and her contacts in the MSS. But that could have put Jensen Huang, Nvidia, and valuable U.S. technology at risk. That wasn’t the only oddity in the administration’s approach to Nvidia. Not long after Trump was first informed about the affair, the U.S. government agreed to allow the sale of some Nvidia chips to China, in exchange for a 25 percent tariff on the transaction. That arrangement, which had no precedent, reversed the administration’s existing policy and ran counter to a long-standing strategy of keeping advanced AI chips out of China. Critics said the administration was helping China get ahead in the AI race, the opposite of what it purported to want. The White House countered that making China more dependent on American chips was smart policy and would keep the U.S. in the lead. But if the president knew that Nvidia might have had a spy in its midst, why was he helping the company do more business in China? The new Democratic majority in Congress will certainly want answers to that question and the many others that remain in the Huang affair. This article originally referred to Jensen Huang as the CEO of Nvidia. He is the former CEO.

华盛顿多年来一直在争论人工智能（AI）在核指挥和控制中的作用，并为中美关系的军事影响而苦恼。人工智能竞赛。它花更少的时间提出一个不同的问题：如果朝鲜领导人金正恩相信美国即将在通用人工智能领域获得强大、持久的优势，那么他的威慑计算将如何改变？
通用人工智能（AGI）——被定义为在认知任务中与人类表现相匹配的强大智能——可能会进一步破坏已经恶化的核威慑关系的稳定。较弱的非 AGI 能力可能会变得尤其成问题。朝鲜的核态势已经一触即发。如果美国获得通用人工智能或类似通用人工智能的能力，平壤可能会采取一种激进的“使用它或失去它”的心态，因为它担心第一次打击会消除其核武器能力并摧毁其领导层。
至关重要的是，美国实际获得 AGI 以及随后发展威慑无效能力，比朝鲜对美国能力和意图的看法更重要。由于平壤采取了咄咄逼人的核姿态，并对美国的意图持批评、偏执的态度，因此，即使在通用人工智能能力投入使用之前，局势也可能会急剧恶化。因此，应该更多地关注通用人工智能如何打破不对称威慑平衡，尤其是针对平壤。
如果通用人工智能的腾飞真正带来指数级增长，一连串的技术突破可能会刺激前所未有的经济增长和军事能力的扩张，有些人称之为代理战争。在这种情况下，具有通用人工智能能力的国家可能会迅速削弱（甚至消除）非通用人工智能国家的二次打击能力。这种技术飞跃将放大不幸的心理倾向，即在面临损失时变得更容易冒险，这被称为前景理论。
因此，在AGI起飞的情况下，非AGI核武器国家，尤其是实力较弱的国家，可能会担心在不久的将来他们将无法威慑AGI国家。因此，他们可以采取更具攻击性的姿态。当然，这并不是唯一的理性反应，但出于我们稍后将描述的原因，我们认为朝鲜更有可能以额外的侵略性做出反应，而不是通过生存、隐蔽和军控谈判寻求庇护。此外，如果递归自我改进能够实现超级人工智能（ASI）（定义为超越任何人类的能力），那么风险将变得更高，核决策时间将变得更加压缩。
AGI 的后果、时间表和扩散仍然是争论的主题，

Washington has spent years debating the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in nuclear command and control, and agonizing over the military implications of China-U.S. AI competition. It has spent far less time asking a different question: how will North Korean leader Kim Jong Un’s deterrence calculus change if he believes the United States is on the verge of obtaining a powerful, enduring advantage in artificial general intelligence?
Artificial general intelligence (AGI) – defined as powerful intelligence matching human performance across cognitive tasks – could further destabilize nuclear deterrence relationships that are already deteriorating. Weaker, non-AGI powers could become especially problematic. North Korea’s nuclear posture is already on a hair trigger. If the United States obtains AGI or AGI-like capabilities, Pyongyang could adopt an aggressive “use it or lose it” mentality because it fears a first strike that eradicates its nuclear weapons capabilities and decapitates its leadership.
Critically, the United States’ actual acquisition of AGI and the subsequent development of deterrence-nullifying capabilities matters less than North Korea’s perceptions of U.S. capabilities and intent. Because Pyongyang has adopted an aggressive nuclear posture and espouses such a critical, paranoid view of U.S. intentions, the situation could spiral even before AGI capabilities are operational. More attention should therefore be paid to how AGI could upset asymmetric deterrence equilibria, especially vis-à-vis Pyongyang.
If AGI takeoff truly unlocks exponential growth, a cascade of technological breakthroughs could spur unprecedented economic growth and expansion in military capabilities that some have termed agentic warfare. Under this scenario, an AGI-capable power could rapidly erode, if not eliminate, the second strike capabilities of a non-AGI power. This technological leap would amplify the unfortunate psychological tendency to become more risk-prone when facing losses, called prospect theory.
Accordingly, under AGI takeoff, non-AGI nuclear weapons powers, especially the weaker ones, will likely fear a near-future wherein they will be unable to deter the AGI power. They could therefore adopt a more aggressive posture. Of course, this isn’t the only rational reaction, but for reasons we will describe later, we think North Korea is much more likely to respond with extra aggression than it is to seek refuge through survivability, concealment, and arms control negotiations. Moreover, if recursive self-improvement delivers artificial superintelligence (ASI), defined as capabilities exceeding any human, the stakes will become much higher and nuclear decision-making timelines will become even more compressed.
AGI consequences, timelines, and diffusion remain a subject of debate, and key AI breakthroughs may be a business cycle or more away, but the balance of evidence suggests huge capability increases are possible. If scaling laws continue to hold, capabilities will keep rising: announced U.S. AI computing capacity is projected to increase by 239 percent this year alone, according to Federal Reserve staff calculations based on Epoch AI data. By 2030, planned U.S. AI compute would be roughly 35 times mid-2025 levels.
While tech CEOs and investors are incentivized to hype AI advances, models are undeniably improving, and at an impressive rate; the newest models are even proving adept at operating in the physical world. For better and for worse, AI software and hardware capabilities are advancing rapidly. Even artificial intelligence experts themselves have expressed surprise at the pace of innovation and warned of the dangers of unrestricted development.
Strategic deterrence nullification would likely lag AGI by many years, but AI timelines are advancing far faster than most expected. North Korea’s force posture is already changing and new command-and-control safeguards – including human-in-the-loop commitments – may take years to agree upon and implement.
AGI attainment would usher in considerable geopolitical disruptions, including altering the nuclear balance-of-power. China and Russia are of special importance in any AGI scenario. China is a peer competitor of the United States, including in AI, and it possesses the world’s third largest nuclear arsenal; Russia possesses the world’s largest nuclear weapon arsenal (by volume) and continues to face off against the United States in Cold War-style proxy conflict. Either competitor could be incentivized to act aggressively if the U.S. is first to approach AGI attainment.
Nevertheless, the gravest AGI-related dangers may come from less-capable nuclear powers, especially North Korea. That’s because Pyongyang has adopted a uniquely aggressive and decentralized form of nuclear command and control, has an aggressive nuclear doctrine, suffers from severe technical and even geographic disadvantages, and it maintains a paranoid disposition towards the United States. Faced with the prospect of losing second strike capability, it could therefore choose to adopt an even riskier posture or operationalize half-baked tech into its nuclear command, control, and communications before the United States crosses the AGI threshold.
Nuclear stability requires mutual vulnerability. China and Russia are more likely to continue to hold the U.S. hostage via threat of retaliation even if the U.S. obtains AGI first; for North Korea, that is much less likely.
AGI Takeoff, or Perceived Takeoff, Upends Conventional and Strategic Military Calculations
If AGI takeoff occurs, its technological, economic, and military consequences will be extremely hard to forecast. Physical constraints and hardware bottlenecks, including in critical minerals, could slow the transformation of software breakthroughs into weapons. Still, powerful AI could rapidly deliver unprecedented economic and technological capacity, which would then translate into military capabilities, including early warning, detection, targeting, and delivery. These capabilities could credibly threaten other states’ second-strike forces.
As the decision window shrinks, mutual vulnerability – the foundation of a stable deterrence relationship – will erode. Given the dangers of facing an AGI-empowered rival, and their own weak monitoring and verification capabilities, non-AGI powers like Pyongyang will watch anxiously for signs that an adversary’s AGI attainment could unlock the potential for a decapitation strike that wipes out their leadership and nuclear capabilities in one fell swoop.
In this scenario, facing rapidly deteriorating strategic options, a state could be motivated to automate nuclear retaliation. They might hope that the dead man’s hand would serve as a final guarantor of deterrence. But as human operators are pulled further out of the nuclear decision-making process, the ethical and practical problems will begin to multiply. History has proven that humans are the last best defense against needless escalation. That was the case in 1983 when a Soviet early warning system erroneously signaled an incoming U.S. intercontinental ballistic missile. Using his knowledge of the faulty system and U.S. strategy, Lieutenant Colonel Stanislav Petrov deduced that the warning was a false positive. He was right: the system’s satellites misread sunlight reflecting off clouds.
In addition, North Korea – and other non-AGI actors – might seek to establish deterrence via other asymmetric methods, such as pre-positioning chemical and biological weapons or developing new, AI-enabled variants. North Korea is thought to have a substantial inventory of both chemical and biological weapons, and it might lean on these capabilities if it fears its nuclear deterrent is compromised.
To limit near-term biological risks from Pyongyang, both Washington and Beijing should closely examine the AI-biology nexus, an asymmetrical threat that North Korea might find compelling to develop if it believed a rival was on the cusp of AGI acquisition. Limiting the risk of North Korea – or other state and non-state actors – may require constraining the publicly-accessible biological capabilities of future releases of large language models. Unsafeguarded models, known as open-weight models, pose the most severe risks. As unsafeguarded models become more capable, virtually anyone can access powerful, unconstrained AI by removing safeguards with relatively little compute.
North Korea is already likely operating unsafeguarded models to exploit zero-day vulnerabilities, as the $6 billion Binance hack suggests. Given the growing risks of AI-designed viruses, including from Pyongyang, Beijing and Washington should have candid conversations about the desirability of diffusing powerful AI capabilities in biology.
North Korea Is Uniquely Vulnerable and Aggressive
Unlike China or Russia, which have large nuclear arsenals, mature intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance capabilities, and demonstrated technological ability to innovate, North Korea’s vulnerability and its aggressive posture may render it the most dangerous nuclear actor in an AGI sprint scenario. Furthermore, unlike China or Russia, countries that can rely on second-strike deterrents due to their deep interiors and nuclear-armed submarines, North Korea lacks a credibly survivable nuclear submarine deterrent.
Finally, North Korea’s own eagerness to adopt AI-enabled weapons will color its perception of adversary intent and the threat posed by AGI. The nuclear deterrence equilibrium on the Korean Peninsula is already fragile; inviting one more destabilizing element may be the straw that breaks the camel’s back.
North Korea’s military is embracing AI with a speed that suggests it is throwing caution to the wind. In 2024, the General Staff Department of the Korean People’s Army created an Electronic Warfare and AI Operation Command to develop and adopt “AI-based electronic warfare support systems.” In August 2025, the Korean People’s Army issued orders to its Strategic Force to “integrate AI-based unified management systems for storing, operating, and commanding nuclear weapons, as well as launching nuclear counterattacks,” according to Daily NK. At the Ninth Party Congress in February of this year, North Korea announced additional plans to integrate AI into its civil and military systems. Since then, even more developments have been announced.
Leader Kim Jong Un himself jumped behind the wheel of a mobile rocket launcher, claiming that the nuclear-capable 600-mm multiple rocket launcher (KN-25) features artificial intelligence in its guidance systems. One month later, Kim oversaw a test of AI-enabled attack and reconnaissance drones, saying, “unmanned equipment and artificial intelligence should be top-prioritized… in modernizing the armed forces.” In May, North Korean media claimed that the military tested a tactical cruise missile that utilizes artificial intelligence for target acquisition and terminal guidance. Despite this appetite for integrating AI across military technologies, limitations in hardware, data, and infrastructure will likely constrain the rollout. These limitations could also produce defects that imperil safeguards meant to stop an unintentional escalation spiral.
Further aggravating the situation, North Korea’s nuclear doctrine is uniquely aggressive and opaque. The country’s rubber stamp parliament passed legislation in 2022 that legitimizes preemptive nuclear attacks under certain conditions. The North will launch a nuclear attack “automatically and immediately” if Kim’s command is threatened, if “a fatal military attack” on critical targets is imminent, or if needed to reclaim “the initiative in war.” The law also outlined a delegative command authority: “Rather than await direct orders from Kim Jong Un, field commanders may now follow predetermined launch plans to release nuclear weapons.” These doctrinal reforms were reinforced by a 2026 constitutional revision that codified the decentralized command authority. Combined with a surge in the production and forward deployment of tactical nuclear weapons, these changes add coherence and credibility to Kim’s first-use strategy, which aims to achieve a maximum deterrence effect through aggression and ambiguity. However, the blurry red lines and threats of preemption are risky and escalatory.
An AGI scenario could lead to further brinksmanship. As Keir A. Lieber and Daryl G. Press noted in a 2017 analysis, “The New Era of Counterforce,” states facing wealthy, technologically advanced adversaries will find it “increasingly difficult to secure their arsenals” as advances in sensors, data processing, and AI erode the conditions that have historically protected second-strike forces.
Pyongyang cannot rule out that an AGI-powered United States will develop next-generation technologies, such as airborne directed energy weapons, highly effective anti-ballistic missile defense, and orbital and sub-orbital weapons. Pyongyang’s weak early warning and intelligence capabilities will amplify the leadership’s fear that its second strike has been rendered moot, especially given its unique vulnerabilities. Nor can Washington easily reassure North Korea: even if the United States integrates AI cautiously into its own nuclear command, control, and communications and is transparent about human-in-the-loop safeguards, a leadership this distrustful could conclude that the AGI moment has arrived and act accordingly.
It is possible that, faced with such daunting odds, North Korea could choose a path of survivability, restraint, and even reconciliation. That would be a rational reaction to this newfound unfavorable position. However, given Pyongyang’s nuclear posture, its historical record, and the leadership’s consistent commitment to robust nuclear capabilities, it is much more likely that Pyongyang will double down on its “escalate to de-escalate” doctrine by adopting even riskier and more aggressive measures.
Fearing a super-capable U.S. and preoccupied with the threat of a decapitation strike, Pyongyang could be more likely to accept the downstream risks that come from adding AI-enabled processes. The first effort would be into their own nuclear command, control, and communications architecture, including early warning systems, targeting, command, control, communications, and navigation. Given North Korea’s already aggressive and risky posture, this embrace of AI can only increase the likelihood that an accidental clash could spiral into a full-on nuclear exchange. In addition, any attack on the North Korean infrastructure supporting the Korean People’s Army AI electronic warfare systems could be interpreted as a nuclear-level aggression, leading to a nuclear-level reprisal.
The efficacy of AI systems is limited by the quality of training data, sensory input, and processing power. In North Korea’s case, the quality of all three is extremely limited. This could produce false positives, which become exponentially more dangerous as humans are removed from the decision-making process. Pairing super-compressed decision timelines with automated attack protocols makes it difficult for a cool-headed human to steer the situation away from crisis. That’s doubly the case when the two states in question lack diplomatic relations, crisis communications, or confidence building measures.
Contrary to popular depictions – including Annie Jacobsen’s book “Nuclear War: A Scenario” and Kathryn Bigelow’s 2025 film “A House of Dynamite” – North Korea’s leadership understands well that launching a pre-emptive strike would be suicidal. But the alarming truth is that Pyongyang could make much more subtle and obscure posture changes that would dramatically increase the chance of accidental escalation. Facing an AGI-enabled United States, North Korea would be much more likely to hastily operationalize half-baked AI nuclear command, control, and communications, hedge with chemical and biological weapons, forward deploy additional assets, engage in gray zone attacks, and engage in aggression that blurs the line between nuclear testing and use, such as an atmospheric test near Korea or Japan that produces no casualties. They may also expand the list of red line items that trigger field commanders to independently launch a nuclear strike.
The United States faces a complex optimization problem: staying ahead of Chinese AI development while managing the nuclear deterrence instability that AGI could unleash, and the potential existential risks of AI itself. Policymakers should begin examining and counteracting these risks now, instead of scrambling in a takeoff scenario. Constraining Chinese access to advanced semiconductors is necessary but not sufficient. U.S. policymakers must also consider how their own AGI development will affect deterrence calculus in other capitals and explore voluntary restraints on capabilities that would destabilize fragile nuclear equilibria.
The next frontier of arms control should include a “human in the loop” clause such as the one featured in the 2024 agreement between the United States and China. The U.S. should lead a multilateral effort to secure buy in from all nuclear powers to commit to the same provisions and more – to wall off as much higher-function nuclear command, control, and communications from automaticity as possible. While it may seem counter-intuitive to consider that Pyongyang would accept limitations on its nuclear program, participation in such a multilateral agreement with the world’s nuclear powers might actually bestow upon it the kind of international legitimacy that Kim craves. And this sort of legitimacy is categorically different from prior offerings because it would situate North Korea among nuclear superpowers on an equitable basis, a tantalizing prospect for Kim that cannot be easily dismissed.
While some may criticize such an effort on the grounds of creating a dangerous precedent by tacitly accepting Pyongyang’s nuclear status, the time has come to stop tilting at “denuclearization” windmills in favor of achieving a material threat reduction, as one of us has argued previously. To be sure, convincing the distrustful leadership in Pyongyang to voluntarily accept limitations on its nuclear program will not be an easy sell. But the costs of inaction are so high and the alternatives so disagreeable that, in the land of lousy policy options, this is an endeavor worthy of focus, energy, and political capital.
Beijing could play a role in containing nuclear-related and asymmetric biological risks. Given the risks of powerful AI diffusing biological research capabilities, and enabling an asymmetric counter to AGI, both the U.S. and China have an interest in constraining AI’s publicly-accessible biological capabilities. The same applies to limiting North Korea’s nuclear capabilities. As during the Six Party Talks, Beijing should be recruited to support Pyongyang’s engagement and implementation.
Over time, such a framework could begin to eat away at the distrust that fuels North Korea’s paranoia and spurs its aggressive nuclear posture. If Kim Jong Un continues to reject good faith efforts, then the U.S. and its allies South Korea and Japan should invest substantially and collaboratively on missile defense architecture and other capabilities needed to address the threat and maintain deterrence. That consequence should incentivize China to act responsibly.

content:
资料照片：美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在美国弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿国家公墓出席“退伍军人节”纪念仪式。(2026年11月11日)
美国总统特朗普将于下星期二(11月17日)开始对菲律宾首都马尼拉进行为期两天的访问，先后参加四方安全对话(Quad)领导人峰会及东南亚国家联盟(ASEAN)特别峰会。白宫称总统在马尼拉参加的一系列会晤，旨在“巩固美国在自由开放的印太地区的领导地位”。
特朗普在2017年、2025年都曾参加ASEAN峰会，至于Quad峰会则是首次参与。Quad由美国、印度、日本和澳大利亚组成。
战略与国际研究中心费里曼中国研究讲座主任埃德加·卡根(Edgard Kagan)9日在一场简报会上表示，在本届政府任期内一直未能举行Quad领导人会议，主因在于美印关系紧张。他认为，特朗普现在决定参加峰会，有助于修复与印度的关系。
在“美国优先”的保护主义政策之下，特朗普政府祭出关税大棒，对印度的出口商品与经贸政策造成强烈冲击。此外，印度因为购买俄罗斯石油而遭到美国批评，甚至因此被施加惩罚性关税。
特朗普首度参与峰会，虽然象征Quad机制运作如常，以及华府和新德里愿意暂时放下芥蒂，不过分析人士普遍不看好这次峰会能端出具体成果，也对美印关系回温程度有所保留。
日本秋田国际教养大学全球研究学程副教授陈宥桦指出，印度政治菁英们对于特朗普过去两年来对印度的施压与忽略一直有诸多不满，以至于QUAD领袖会谈就算举行可能也很难产出什么实质的成果。
台湾清华大学印度中心主任方天赐接受美国之音采访时表示，印度原本是去年Quad峰会主办国，只是因为特朗普不愿意去印度，最后不了了之，现在虽然恢复举办，但印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪(Narendra Modi)心里难免不是滋味。
印度金尔德全球大学国际事务学院副教授潘孟吉(Manoj Kumar Panigrahi)向美国之音表示：“这是一个重新建立联系的好机会，但我怀疑它能否带来实质成果。特朗普肯定会推动与印度就目前搁置的贸易协定进行谈判；而对印度来说，重点将是签证规定以及进一步加强国防关系。”
战略与国际研究中心的卡根指出，Quad领导人会议得以在特朗普访华前召开，也是在向中国国家主席习近平释放信息：美国与一些国家有着非常重要的关系，同时表明总统正在努力改善美印关系。他说，经历了中期选举的失利，这场峰会将大大提振特朗普访华前的信心。
潘孟吉认为，鉴于峰会将在马尼拉举行，中国咄咄逼人的举动肯定会被提及，但很可能不会直接点名中国。考量到对地主的尊重，这场峰会或许也会促使四方安全对话机制在海上安全和领土完整方面支持菲律宾和东盟。
方天赐则表示，四方安全对话起初的战略意涵，主要是为了抗衡中国影响力，只是当前时空环境不同，而且特朗普下一步就要前往中国深圳参加亚太经合会(APEC)，可以预期不会对中国有太过尖锐的批评。四方安全对话也会从美国设计的传统安全的导向，走向更多非传统安全的合作领域。
他说：“美国特朗普政府，还有澳大利亚，甚至印度都希望能重新跟中国维持一个比较友好稳定的关系。目前成员国里面只有日本跟中国的关系比较紧张，所以即便现在举行这个峰会，它等于是说不太会像过去一样那么强调反中的立场。”
路透社星期六引述知情人士的话指出，关键矿产供应以及确保商业航道预计将列入峰会议程。
分析人士指出，Quad领袖峰会重启让日本松了一口气，不仅是这项机制最早是由日本前首相安倍晋三所提出，而且日本在过去一年以来承受着北京对其“军国主义”复甦的指责压力。
日媒共同社星期六报道，在日中关系持续恶化的背景下，日本希望借由多边会议摸索改善双边关系的希望变得渺茫。
共同社报道称日本首相高市早苗很可能和赴马尼拉参加东盟峰会的中国总理李强擦身而过，至于在深圳借APEC峰会和习近平会晤的工作安排同样进展不顺。
卡根说，高市将与特朗普总统、莫迪总理以及澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴尼斯(Anthony Albanese)会面，对日本而言意义重大。
陈宥桦告诉美国之音：“高市政府一直在努力的就是用各种方式营造出高市与特朗普的个人关系很稳固之形象，现在正努力促进着高市与特朗普能够在美中俄会谈之前先见一次面，既使这次的见面可能不会比美中俄会谈产生更多的实质成果，但会起到稳定日本国内政治的作用。”

title: Taiwan Indigenous farmer revives climate-resilient millet
zh_title: 台湾本土农民复兴气候适应型小米
summary: 台湾东南部的原住民农民巴努·伊斯马哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 走过一片金色的高秆田，用手收割一种能够抵抗极端天气的古老作物的谷粒。 2026 年 10 月 21 日，台湾农民巴努·伊斯马哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 在台东将刚收获的油小米摊开在阳光下晒干。照片：I-Hwa Cheng/AFP 台湾原住民农民曾种植油小米，以防主粮枯死，但 60 多年前，随着水稻变得更加容易获得，油小米基本上从田间消失了。在过去的十年里，伊斯玛哈桑和他年迈的父母一直致力于复兴几乎被遗忘的地方。
content:
台湾东南部的原住民农民巴努·伊斯马哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 走过一片金色的高秆田，用手收割一种能够抵抗极端天气的古老作物的谷粒。 2026 年 10 月 21 日，台湾农民巴努·伊斯马哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 在台东将刚收获的油小米摊开在阳光下晒干。照片：I-Hwa Cheng/AFP 台湾原住民农民曾种植油小米，以防主粮枯死，但 60 多年前，随着水稻变得更加容易获得，油小米基本上从田间消失了。在过去的十年里，伊斯马哈桑和他年迈的父母一直在台东县布克拉武村的布农社区努力恢复几乎被遗忘的农作物。 “我们只是希望带回许多传统的布农族作物，并再次在这片土地上种植它们，”48岁的伊斯马哈桑在晴朗的蓝天下的油小米田里告诉法新社。油小米，即布农语中的“莳萝”，是台湾特有的植物，可以在山上野生生长。伊斯玛哈桑首先在网上了解到这种植物，然后开始自己的研究，梳理历史文献并与部落长老交谈，其中包括一位记得上次吃这种植物是在半个世纪前的妇女。他发现，布农族农民过去常常在种植主要作物谷子的同时种植油小米，作为收成歉收或发生灾害时的“后备”。经过多年亲自种植油小米，伊斯玛哈桑开始明白为什么他的祖先依赖这种作物。
一粒油小米种子可以长出 15 至 20 个圆锥花序或分枝种子簇，并且茎可以自行再生，而谷子通常每粒种子长出一个圆锥花序，必须在切割后重新播种。事实证明，当极端天气或疾病爆发破坏了他 2.2 公顷（5.4 英亩）的农场时，它比谷子更坚强。伊斯马哈桑说，几年前一场持续了 200 多天的干旱期间，油小米“保持鲜绿色”，而其他作物却枯萎了。台风、洪水，甚至锈病爆发也没有影响到它。台湾中央研究院退休教授、植物遗传学专家邢月娥15年前在一个国际论坛上第一次听说了油小米。幸不知道的是，1890 年代采集的台湾油粟标本就存放在英国皇家植物园 (Kew)。兴带领一个研究小组在台湾东南部的山区找到了油小米，并开始研究这种鲜为人知的谷物。她发现，种子的保护性蜡涂层使其无需灌溉、化肥或杀虫剂即可生长，即使在质量较差的土地上也是如此。 2026 年 10 月 21 日，台湾农民 Linkav Ismahasan 在台东的一块田里收割油小米。照片：I-Hwa Cheng / 法新社 油小米富含油、蛋白质和矿物质，可用于人类和动物消费，也可用作燃料。 “它在利用阳光和水方面自然非常有效，”辛说。
“至于土壤条件，即使是在地面布满大石头的山区，它也能生长得很好。” “非常珍贵”伊斯马哈桑从一粒油小米开始了他的种植。现在，这个家庭每年在他们种植其他传统布农谷类作物的土地上每年收获两次油小米。油小米个头小，无味，可以用来做粥、馒头、面包，甚至爆米花。但该家族一直在努力说服其他农民种植这种植物，因为它在商业上尚不可行。油粟不仅是劳动密集型产业，而且意义重大

【原文 English Original】
Indigenous farmer Banu Ismahasan walks through a golden field of tall stalks in southeastern Taiwan , harvesting by hand the grain heads of an ancient crop resistant to extreme weather. Taiwan farmer Banu Ismahasan spreads freshly harvested oil millet out to dry in the sun in Taitung on October 21, 2026. Photo: I-Hwa Cheng / AFP Once grown by Indigenous farmers in Taiwan in case their staple crops died, oil millet largely disappeared from fields more than 60 years ago as rice became more available. Over the past decade, Ismahasan and his elderly parents have worked to revive the nearly forgotten crop in the Bunun community in Buklavu, a village surrounded by lush green mountains in Taitung county. “We just hope to bring back many traditional Bunun crops and grow them on this land again,” Ismahasan, 48, told AFP in his oil millet field under a clear blue sky. Oil millet, or “dill” in the Bunun language, is endemic to Taiwan and can be found growing wild in the mountains. Ismahasan first read about the plant online and then embarked on his own research, combing through historical documents and speaking to tribal elders, including a woman who recalled last eating it half a century ago. He discovered that Bunun farmers used to grow oil millet alongside their staple crop foxtail millet as a “back-up” when harvests failed or disasters hit. After years of growing oil millet himself, Ismahasan came to understand why his ancestors relied on the crop. A single oil millet seed can grow 15 to 20 panicles, or branching seed clusters, and the stems regenerate on their own, while foxtail millet typically grows one panicle per seed and must be sown again after being cut. It has also proven hardier than foxtail millet when extreme weather or disease outbreaks have ravaged his 2.2-hectare (5.4-acre) farm. During a drought several years ago that lasted more than 200 days, the oil millet “stayed bright green” while other crops withered, Ismahasan said. Typhoons, floods and even a rust disease outbreak have not affected it either. Hsing Yue-ie, a retired professor from Taiwan’s Academia Sinica and an expert in plant genetics, first heard of oil millet 15 years ago at an international forum. Unbeknownst to Hsing, specimens of Taiwan oil millet collected in the 1890s were sitting in Britain’s Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew. Hsing led a research team to find oil millet in the mountains of southeastern Taiwan and began studying the little-known cereal. She found that the seed’s protective wax coating enabled it to grow without irrigation, fertilisers or pesticides, even on poor-quality land. Taiwan farmer Linkav Ismahasan harvests oil millet in a field in Taitung on October 21, 2026. Photo: I-Hwa Cheng / AFP Rich in oil, protein and minerals, it can be used for human and animal consumption, as well as for fuel. “It’s naturally very efficient at using sunlight and water,” said Hsing. “As for soil conditions, even in mountainous areas where the ground is full of large rocks, it can still grow very well.” ‘Very precious’ Ismahasan started his crop with one panicle of oil millet. The family now harvests oil millet twice a year on a section of their property where they grow other traditional Bunun cereal crops. Tiny and tasteless, oil millet can be used in porridge, steamed buns, bread and even popcorn. But the family has struggled to convince other farmers to grow it because it is not yet commercially viable. Oil millet is not only labour intensive but also significantly more expensive for consumers than rice, by far Taiwan’s most popular staple. While the current market for oil millet is limited, Taiwan’s National Crop Germplasm Center sees value in preserving its seeds for the future, when climate change might force more farmers to consider growing the crop. Oil millet seeds are “very precious” because of their genetic diversity and ability to adapt to the environment, Lin Yen-yu, an assistant researcher at the centre, told AFP. Seeds are kept in aluminium foil packets and stored at -18C under low-moisture conditions where they can last for decades, Lin said. “In the future, when cultivation methods or climate change undergo certain shifts, their value may start to be recognised and discovered,” he said. “It preserves many possibilities.” Ismahasan said his priority for now was to get more people in his community growing and eating oil millet, bringing “it back into our everyday lives, just as it was for our elders”. “If we don’t even eat it ourselves anymore, how can we expect to turn it into a viable business?” he said.

summary: Fundraiser by KIMA Network Inc : Flash Flood Rasuwa Children’s Relief Fund Rasuwa Children’s Relief ensures orphans get housing, food, and education after the floods KIMA Network Inc is organizing this fundraiser to benefit Kima Network Inc
content:
Fundraiser by KIMA Network Inc : Flash Flood Rasuwa Children’s Relief Fund
Rasuwa Children’s Relief ensures orphans get housing, food, and education after the floods
KIMA Network Inc is organizing this fundraiser to benefit Kima Network Inc.
KIMA Network is raising funds to support school-age children from Syabru Besi, Setang, Timure, and surrounding communities affected by the flooding.
Because search and rescue efforts are still ongoing, we do not want to make assumptions about any child's family situation. We continue to hope that missing parents and loved ones will be found and reunited with their families.
Our action plan: We collected data from 5 boarding schools in Kathmandu and identified 41 students who are orphaned or have lost a parent, and who have no sponsor or only partial sponsorship. We have decided to sponsor all 41 students for this year and the upcoming so they can stay safe, supported, and in school. The schools are:
• Srongtsen Bhrikuti Boarding High School
• North Valley English Secondary Boarding School
We still have a waiting list of children who need a sponsor. Please reach out to us or support through GoFundMe to help the children of Rasuwa.
We want to be there for them not only in the immediate aftermath, but in the months and years that follow.
For any child who is ultimately left without parental care, surviving the disaster will only be the beginning. They will need stability. They will need an education. They will need a safe place to live. And, most of all, they will need the reassurance that they have not been forgotten.
• Safe housing, food, clothing, and everyday necessities
• School tuition, uniforms, books, and educational expenses
• Longer-term assistance for children left without parents or stable caregivers
Our commitment is not only to help these children through the immediate crisis, but to give them the stability, education, and support they need to move forward.
You do not have to be from Nepal to make a difference. Whether you are able to donate any amount ($) or simply share this fundraiser, every act of support can help us reach a child who may need care for years to come.
Please keep the families of Rasuwa in your thoughts, and if you are able, please stand with the children whose lives may be changed forever by this disaster.
KIMA Network Inc, EIN: 39-4350034
Your easy, powerful, and trusted home for help

content:
Fundraiser by Yangkey Gangshar : Nepal- Tibet Floods: Help a Mountain Guide's Wife & Children
This fund brings food, housing, and school costs to Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and children
Yangkey Gangshar is organizing this fundraiser.
Our family is heartbroken by the devastating floods that swept through communities along the Nepal–Tibet border, destroying homes, livelihoods, and taking many precious lives—including our beloved first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa Dakpu Lama Tamang.
We are Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering, and members of the Gangshar family whose roots are deeply connected to the communities affected by this tragedy. We are raising these funds for our first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and their two young children, who are now facing an unimaginable loss and an uncertain future.
“Cho Cho” is an endearing Tibetan term for an older brother. To our family, Cho Cho Dawa was a beloved husband, father, son, brother, nephew, cousin, and friend.
A Father Who Gave Everything for His Family
At 45 years old, Cho Cho Dawa worked as a mountain guide in Nepal’s Langtang region, providing for his wife and two children. His work often took him away from home for weeks or months at a time, but he took great pride in what he did. He was known for his warmth, kindness, generosity, and joyful spirit.
Tragically, the mountains he knew so well and worked in to support his family became the place where he lost his life.
He leaves behind his wife and two young children—a daughter, 11, and a son, 7. They are now facing not only the devastating loss of their husband and father, but the uncertainty of rebuilding their lives without the person who provided for their family.
The picture attached captures Cho Cho Dawa with his family dressed in our traditional Tibetan attire while celebrating Losar, the Tibetan New Year.
Our Family’s Connection to This Community
Our connection to this region goes back generations.
Our father and his family originally came from Kyidong (Kyirong, སྐྱིད་གྲོང་) in Tibet, a place now often referred to as Gyirong in international news. In 1959, our grandparents and relatives were forced to flee Tibet and eventually found refuge and a new home in the border regions of Nepal.
Our father and his siblings grew up in the Syabru besi and Briddhim communities, where they went to school, formed lifelong friendships, and began rebuilding their lives after leaving Tibet. These communities became an important part of our family’s history and home in Nepal.
The school where our father and his siblings once studied was among the places devastated by the floods.
Yangkey was fortunate to visit Syabru besi and Briddhim in March 2014 and again with Choenyi in November 2025. During those visits, she spent time with Cho Cho Dawa, his wife, mother, and brother and was warmly welcomed into their home. The pictures included here were taken during those visits and are now incredibly meaningful to our family.
The pictures also show places we saw and experienced during our November 2025 visit. One shows a hydropower facility along the road to Syabru besi which has been damanged and another shows the homes, guesthouses, and local businesses in Syabru besi, many of which have since been washed away.
Our family was once forced to leave our homeland in Tibet and found a place in Nepal where generations of our family could rebuild their lives. Now, that same community has been devastated by another unimaginable tragedy.
What took generations to build was swept away in moments. But the lives, memories, and stories connected to these places remain.
Cho Cho Dawa is not the only loss our family is mourning.
His brother, Cho Cho Tsering, is also facing unimaginable grief, as members of his wife’s family were among those tragically swept away.
We are also mourning the many precious lives lost in this devastating tragedy, including relatives, friends, and members of the Tibetan community.
Behind every life lost is a family now facing a future without someone they love.
We are raising funds to directly support Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and two children as they begin rebuilding their lives without him.
The funds will be used specifically for:
Shelter, rent, and household expenses
School-related expenses and future education costs for the children
Medical and other essential family needs that may arise
Long-term support to help the family regain stability and rebuild their lives
100% of the funds raised through this GoFundMe will go directly toward supporting Cho Cho Dawa’s family and, if we are fortunate enough to raise more than is needed for Cho Cho Dawa’s immediate family, additional funds will be used to help other affected families in the Tibetan community of Syabru besi who have lost loved ones, homes, or their livelihoods as a result of this disaster.
Yangkey will be traveling to Nepal in approximately two weeks and plans to personally deliver the funds raised directly to the affected families. The funds will be used solely for the relief, essential needs, and family-support purposes described above.
We want to make sure the support reaches those who need it most and provides meaningful help during this incredibly difficult time.
Every donation, no matter the amount, can make a meaningful difference.
If you are unable to donate, please consider sharing this fundraiser with your friends, family, coworkers, and community. A share may help this story reach someone who is able to help.
Thank you for taking the time to hear Cho Cho Dawa’s story and for standing with his wife and children, our family, and the communities affected by this devastating tragedy.
From our family to yours, thank you for your kindness, compassion, love, and support.
Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering & Gangshar Family
“The basic foundation of humanity is compassion and love.”

content:
Fundraiser by Tarra Subhar Massallo : Immediate aid for families affected by the Nepal-Tibet Flood
This fund provides direct aid for shelter, food, and essentials to Nepal-Tibet families
Tarra Subhar Massallo is organizing this fundraiser.
After fleeing from the Chinese annexation of Tibet, many Kyirong Tibetan families crossed into Nepal believing their exile would be temporary. It was not. Syabrubesi and the Trishuli valley had become their home instead- a place where hundreds of families had to rebuild from nothing, including my grandparents. Like many Tibetan refugees, they eventually moved on to build new lives in India. However, not everyone left. Some of their family stayed behind in Syabrubesi and the Trishuli valley, carrying on the roots left behind by previous generations.
On August 26, 2026, a glacier collapse high in the Langtang Himal sent a wall of water and debris surging down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli Bazaar: the towns where that branch of our family stayed and built their lives after losing everything once before. Four households in our family were directly affected:
Our cousin Dawa Dakpa (confirmed deceased) leaves behind a wife and two young children.
Aku Jangchup, his wife, and child (confirmed deceased)
Nama Nangsa Ghongma's family and relatives (missing)
Nama Karmo Subhar's family and relatives (missing)
Now, our families face rebuilding once again, with roads and homes submerged in mud. 100% of every contribution will go directly to these impacted families and the wider flood-affected communities as they recover together. The funds will be spent on various essentials based on each family's needs (including, but not limited to: temporary shelter, food, emergency medical care, and transportation costs). We invite you to help write the next chapter of this story. Please help support this fundraiser in any way that you can.
My name is Tarra Subhar Massallo. I am the granddaughter of Tibetan refugees who fled from Kyirong during the 1959 Chinese annexation of Tibet, and the daughter of a Tibetan immigrant mother who moved from India to the United States with her family in search of a better life. Growing up in a mixed household, I am surrounded by the importance of my many cultures and giving back to my respective communities.

content:
Fundraiser by Dominic Urso : Help Bhujung Rebuild After the Tibet-Nepal Flood
Bhujung’s fund covers urgent food, shelter, and essentials lost in the recent Syabru Besi flood
Dominic Urso is organizing this fundraiser.
Dominic and Kayla are raising funds for Bhujung Tamang, a friend they met while traveling in Nepal before/after the Langtang trek. During that trip, Dominic and Kayla stayed with Bhujung for a few days in his village of Syabru Besi. Bhujung welcomed them with kindness and gave them a truly special local experience they have never forgotten. Now, after a devastating flood destroyed Syabru Besi, Bhujung is facing an unimaginable loss. His home and hotel were destroyed, many of his friends were killed or are missing, and he lost all of his possessions in the disaster. It is estimated that Syabru Besi still has 1300 people missing.
Dominic and Kayla met Bhujung by chance while starting their 7 day hike up the Langtang Valley, one of Nepal's premier hiking destinations. They were looking for a place to stay and found the only hotel in the Old Village of Syabru Besi. Upon getting to know Bhujung, Dominic and Kayla discovered that they were the first guests Bhujung had had in almost 3 years because he was taking care of his late mother's declining health. As a token of gratitude and friendship, Bhujung gifted Dominic and Kayla a hand stitched bag his mother made pictured above.
This fundraiser is meant to provide direct relief to Bhujung as he begins the long process of recovering and rebuilding after this tragedy. The money raised will go directly to him to help support his immediate needs (food, housing, etc.) and give him a foundation to move forward after losing so much. Dominic and Kayla are asking for donations of any amount to help Bhujung through this heartbreaking time. If you are able to give, thank you for showing compassion and support to someone who once showed such generosity to travelers far from home. Please consider donating and sharing this fundraiser to help Bhujung rebuild his life.

content:
Fundraiser by Craig De Meillon : Support Craig’s Mission to Aid Nepal Tibet Mudslide Victims
Craig’s campaign funds deployment, equipment, and communications for mudslide rescue work
Craig De Meillon is organizing this fundraiser.
My name is Craig De Meillon, and I am based in Miami, Florida. I work in safety and emergency management and am a trained firefighter and EMT with professional experience responding to disasters, emergencies, and humanitarian situations.
I am raising these funds as an independent volunteer to support my deployment to the areas affected by the recent mudslides and flooding in Nepal near the China border. I am not a family member or representative of anyone affected by the disaster, nor am I collecting these funds on behalf of a government agency or other organization. I am responding independently based on my emergency-response experience and my ability to bring useful communications and search equipment into the field.
The funds raised will be used primarily to cover the direct costs of my deployment and emergency-response work. This includes my airfare and ground transportation to and within the affected region, accommodation and essential field logistics, food and other necessary expenses while deployed, and emergency-response equipment and supplies.
A significant part of the funding will also be used for search and communications capabilities. This may include purchasing or renting drones that can be used to conduct aerial searches, assess inaccessible areas, locate people who may be stranded or missing, and help response teams understand conditions on the ground. Funds will also be used for satellite communications equipment and associated Starlink service costs so that I can maintain reliable communications in areas where local telecommunications infrastructure may be damaged, unavailable, or overloaded.
Where practical, I may purchase essential supplies locally rather than transporting them from the United States. This allows funds to be used more efficiently and can also support local businesses and responders.
The primary beneficiary of this fundraiser is me, Craig De Meillon, because the funds are being raised to cover the actual expenses I incur while independently deploying and carrying out this emergency-response work. The money is not being raised for personal profit or general living expenses. It is intended to offset the costs directly associated with the mission, including travel, equipment, communications, transportation, and necessary field expenses.
Once on the ground, I will coordinate as appropriate with local emergency responders, humanitarian organizations, community leaders, and other response personnel to determine where my skills, equipment, and communications capabilities can be most useful. My role and activities may change depending on the needs identified in the affected areas and the accessibility and safety of the region.
I will keep records of mission-related expenses and provide updates throughout the deployment so donors can understand how the funds are being used and what work is being carried out on the ground.
Thank you to everyone who contributes, shares this fundraiser, or supports the response in any way. Every contribution helps make it possible for me to get the equipment, communications, and resources needed to reach affected areas and assist where I can. Flood

content:
Fundraiser by Kurshat Uyghur : Support Uyghur film & tell the story together
Kurshat Uyghur is organizing this fundraiser.
We've been making preparation for this film for nearly a year. It is a story of a young Uyghur man’s life in exile after losing contact with his family members. We have received funding from a few organizations, but not quite enough for the entire production process. So we decided to ask for help from those of you who care about the Uyghurs and the work that we’re doing. Our goal is to reach $10,000.
If you have any interest in Uyghur culture or the Uyghur film industry, then please consider a contribution. Your small act of kindness will greatly enhance this film, you will not be disappointed. This film will open your eyes to stories from a beautiful and marginalized people group
The film will be released on March 21st, 2023. All donors will be listed in the end credits and receive a steamable/ download link to the film, and donors who give $100 or more contributions will receive special thanks and additional gifts as shown below:
$100 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film and a handwritten thank you letter.
$200 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film, a poster with the director’s signature and a handwritten thank you letter.
$500 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film, a poster with the director’s signature and a handwritten thank you letter also your name will be present on the director's special thanks section ending of the film.
$5000 donation - you will receive all of the above and will be credited as a co-producer.
Shirzat, an Uyghur international student who has just graduated from college in the United States, had big dreams for his future prior to undertaking his education. He had planned to return to his homeland to take over his father's business, marry his long-term girlfriend, build a happy family, and become a successful entrepreneur. But with the sudden implementation of China's arbitrary mass abduction policy, millions of Uyghurs, like his father, were taken and have disappeared. For Shirzat, who wasn’t able to pursue his studies due to the crisis back home, this was tragic. He felt he had been thrown from the sky to the ground. With finances in ruins, his father missing, his family in danger, his relationship hanging by a thread, he soon spiraled into a cloud of depression and compulsive attention to politics. He withdrew from his relationships with his friends and put his life on hold while struggling to overcome his painful reality and searching for hope in the midst of it.
We will work with some of the most talented people around the world. The Director and screenwriter of this film have decades of experience in the industry. He has also made a number of short films while in university, many of which won the best picture of the year at regional and international film festivals. Our core team members are creative-minded people who have participated in numerous film projects. We have absolute confidence that we will work together as one and give the audiences astonishing results.
