Industrial fishing has made Spain and Taiwan the world’s biggest blue shark catchers, but flawed science and political inaction are accelerating overfishing, hurling sharks towards extinction.
By Tristen Taylor, Nathalie Bertrams and Crystal Chow
A shark caught as bycatch lies on the quay at Nanfangao fishing port before being auctioned. Under Taiwanese law, sharks must be landed with their fins naturally attached, prohibiting finning at sea. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)
Refrigerated container trucks are backed up against the Hermanos Fernández Ibáñez fish-processing factory, a bit outside of the Spanish port city of Vigo. Workers open the truck’s doors and, in the near-freezing air, use long fish hooks to pull out clusters of frozen blue sharks and swordfish. All of the sharks are headless. The sharks hit the concrete floor and scatter like a handful of thrown unlucky dice.
Workers cut off the fins, separate the 15 tonnes of blue sharks by weight and then skin them using two-handed drawknives. If they are not stored in the -25°C to -50°C warehouse, the sharks are cut up into loins and small cubes, which are sold in European supermarkets.
The business model for the Spanish shark fishing industry is fairly straightforward: catch the sharks in the Atlantic, Pacific and Indian oceans and sell the meat either inside Europe or to countries such as Brazil and Morocco. The fins and skins go to Asia, where Singapore acts as a major trading hub.
Claudio Ibáñez is in charge of the factory, his grandfather started the business back in 1940, and he sells the shark meat for between R28 and R37/kg and the fins for R280/kg. With the sale of both the meat and fins, each individual shark brings in a revenue of R56/kg. By way of comparison, he gets R93/kg for swordfish, a price he describes as “very cheap”.
Hermanos Fernández Ibáñez isn’t just a fishing processing company, it also has two longline fishing vessels, both of which are currently in the Pacific. Swordfish and blue sharks are caught on the same long lines with the same hooks. The boats stay out in the oceans for years and the crews are flown back to Spain for rotation. The swordfish and blue sharks are landed in foreign ports and shipped to the processing plant in containers. Hermanos Fernández Ibáñez is right at the start of the blue shark value chain.
Ibáñez explains that the company started fishing swordfish 35 years ago. He says that “at that moment we didn’t appreciate the blue shark. Year by year we were catching some blue shark.”
The headquarters of Hermanos Fernández Ibáñez in Vigo. Founded as a fresh fish business about 75 years ago, the family company is now run by its fourth generation and specialises in frozen swordfish, tuna and shark. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)
He explains that at first the price for blue shark was very low. Over time it started to rise to the point where, starting 15 years ago, the blue shark fishery is now, as Ibáñez puts it, “a very good complement to the swordfish fishery.”
In fact, Hermanos Fernández Ibáñez relies on combining the blue sharks and the swordfish fisheries since neither is economically viable on its own. And the company is not alone in fishing for blue sharks. Far from it.
Taiwanese and Spanish fleets catch blue sharks in great numbers.
Blue sharks are a pelagic species found across the world’s oceans and they are one of the most abundant shark species. While their diet ranges considerably, cephalopods such as squid and octopus are an important food source. Blue sharks are the most fecund species of shark: females have litters of 34 pups on average and reproduce annually. That said, blue sharks reproduce more slowly than bony fish and the fecundity of bony fish is proving to be inadequate to compensate for overfishing – 12.7% of all bony fish species face extinction.
In the fishing port of Vigo, regarded as Europe’s largest fishing port for fish landed for human consumption. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)
While great white sharks, orcas, tiger sharks and some sea lions predate upon young blue sharks, human beings are by a long way the main predators of both juvenile and adult blue sharks. According to FishStat, a specialised database belonging to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), 119,820.62 tonnes of blue sharks were caught in 2024.
Of that, Spain caught 45,374.92 tonnes (37.8% of the global catch) and Taiwan 31,890.38 tonnes (26.6%). While no other country comes close to these tonnages, countries like Peru and Namibia play important transit roles. Walvis Bay in Namibia, for example, is an important port for Spanish fishing companies to land and process blue sharks. In 2024, Spain imported 1,725.35 tonnes of blue shark with a value of R30-million from Namibia.
By its own admission, the FAO’s total catch figures are heavily reliant on records from industrial fishing fleets. Discards at sea, small-scale fishing, recreational fishing and other activities are often not recorded. To rectify this and provide an accurate account of fishing, the marine biologist Daniel Pauly formed the organisation Sea Around Us in 1999.
The skin is removed and exported to China, where it is used for leather products. One way it feels almost like velvet, against the grain like sandpaper. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)Only after landing are the fins removed. Shark meat sells for about €1.50 per kilogram, while fins fetch about €15 before being sold on through Spanish traders to Asian markets. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams) Only after landing are the fins removed. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)
Using additional data sources, they were able to re-analyse the data from 1950 to 2019 and concluded that fishing catches in general were 50% more than what reported catches indicate. The peak year for the total global catch of all species was 1996.
The difference between the Sea Around Us findings and the FAO’s reported blue shark catch is considerable. For the 2019 catch, Sea Around Us concluded that a total of 347,229.31 tonnes of blue shark were caught, considerably higher than the FAO’s figure of 109,982.24 tonnes.
The point worth remembering here is that official reported landings don’t represent the actual level of blue shark fishing and of fishing in general.
For example, a study by Hoang Huy Huynh of the National Kaohsiung University of Science and Technology in Taiwan and three other scientists states: “In the Indian Ocean, reported blue shark landings averaged 26,691 tons annually from 2015 to 2019. However, actual catches are likely to exceed 55,000 tons due to inadequate monitoring, misreporting, and illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing.”
A consulting firm, Poseidon, used an estimated average weight of 27kg per shark landed – those sharks that avoid longliners’ hooks and grow to adult males typically weigh between 27kg and 55kg, females between 93kg and 182kg – to arrive at a figure of seven million blue sharks caught in 2019. Poseidon also estimated that the 2019 value of blue shark meat and fins was R6.6-billion.
Shark fins are separated, sorted by size and prepared for trade at Kaohsiung fishing port. The fins are landed together with the carcasses, as required under Taiwan’s regulations.
(Photo: Nathalie Bertrams) Frozen blue sharks from a distant-water fishing vessel are landed at Kaohsiung fishing port, Taiwan. The port is a major base for Taiwan’s longline fleet, where catches are unloaded, weighed and prepared for processing into shark meat and fins.
Using the same average weight and the FAO’s catch figure, we come to the very conservative figure of 4.4 million blue sharks caught in 2024. But that’s not the most startling fact coming out of the FAO’s data. We never used to fish blue sharks at any kind of industrial scale.
In 1950, only one country reported landing blue sharks. Indonesia recorded 47 tonnes and remained the only country fishing them until 1978 when France landed four tonnes. Spain started fishing blue sharks in 1997, landing 29,917 tonnes. Taiwan’s reported catch came a decade later, a haul of 3,399 tonnes. What the data clearly shows is that 1997 was the year when the large-scale industrial fishing of blue sharks kicked off and the Spanish were at the forefront with 75.7% of the total landed catch.
Daniel Pauly, a professor at the University of British Columbia, predicts that the “shark fishery is not going to last long, two decades, perhaps two decades, and then it’s gone”.
After the collapse of the blue shark fishery, Pauly says that “we will start fishing something else. For example, mesopelagics, lantern fish and so on.”
The International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN) placed blue shark on its Red List in 2018, giving the species a “near threatened” designation. In 2022, the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) added blue sharks to its Appendix II listing, which means countries now have to issue export permits.
CITES’ description of the classification is: “Appendix II lists species that are not necessarily now threatened with extinction but that may become so unless trade is closely controlled.”
The IUCN declared in 2024 that blue sharks were “largely depleted”. Its assessment states: “In the long term, with maximum conservation effort, the species’ condition could improve significantly… Achieving this would require strict enforcement of catch limits and a temporary suspension of large-scale commercial fishing in the Mediterranean.”
Back in 2016, the IUCN designated Mediterranean blue sharks as critically endangered, with a population decline of up to 90% over 30 years due to overfishing.
Verdesca alla mediterranea, a well-known Italian dish, is made from blue shark and a simple Google search throws up all kinds of recipes: for example, Elena Terrile’s cooking website, Cucina con Nenè, punts a recipe, as does the Italian frozen food company Emme Gel.
Spain caught two and half tonnes of Mediterranean blue sharks in 2024, according to the FAO.
Angela Cortina is in her office at the Fishing Vessel Owners’ Cooperative of the Port of Vigo (AVRI), an association representing 200 fishing boats. Out of those 200 boats, 30 are longliners that target both swordfish and blue shark. She says that while 2,200 people are directly dependent on swordfish and blue shark, the European Union doesn’t care enough about the industry, which is threatened, in her view, by foreign competitors operating under weaker environmental and labour standards.
She shows us a glossy cookbook featuring dishes such as marinated blue shark carpaccio and grilled blue shark with citrus vinaigrette, apple and pomegranate. ARVI runs an annual seafood festival in Vigo, which promotes blue shark meat, among other marine food sources.
Ángela Cortina, marine biologist and technical secretary at ARVI, the shipowners’ association in Vigo. She argues that European blue shark fisheries are sustainable as long as they operate within EU quotas, CITES regulations and traceability rules.
Blue shark, she says, is “tasteless, basically. The good thing about it is that you can make it taste like you want. It’s fishy but it’s not a very strong taste.”
Cortina is adamant that the Spanish fleet’s blue shark catches are tightly controlled and are ecologically sustainable. According to her and because of their fecundity, blue sharks “recuperate very quickly. They’re very resistant and very resilient as a species. That’s been known and monitored by scientists for a long time. So we know that.”
She adds: “Sometimes it’s problematic because they reproduce so fast and they prey on other species, on smaller fish. If they are in the longline, they will go for the swordfish. So the species is monitored in every area of the world.”
The regional fishing management organisation (RFMO) for both the North Atlantic and Southern Atlantic is the International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas (ICCAT) and its sets quotas for blue shark: a total allowable catch of 30,000 tonnes for the North Atlantic and 27,711 tonnes for the South Atlantic. The European Union is granted the bulk of the quota, getting 62.8% of the South Atlantic quota and 82.6% from the North Atlantic.
One important thing to note about the Atlantic quotas is that they are higher than the current level of fishing in the Atlantic. In other words, the quotas are not restricting blue shark fishing and future increases in the level of fishing are entirely possible.
The situation is a bit different in the Indian and Pacific oceans, where both Spain and Taiwan fish hard. The RFMOs for these areas have not set quotas, so it’s open season on the sharks.
The individual RFMOs for the Pacific, Indian and Atlantic oceans all state that their blue shark fisheries are sustainable according to science – that there is no danger of the stock collapsing like so many other fisheries have done – and this is where things become murky, complicated and downright surreal.
Retailer holding shark skin in Taipeh, Taiwan. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)
The basic process of determining the sustainability of the fisheries is that a scientific committee attached to each RFMO assesses the stock and then makes recommendations to the countries that constitute the RFMO. These countries then make a consensus-based decision on the recommendations. If any one country disagrees with the recommendations, they won’t be taken up.
Practically speaking, this means that setting a quota, changing a quota limit or instituting some other fishing restriction is difficult because of competing interests between countries and a strong desire to protect national fishing industries.
In essence, the decisions on what an RFMO should or shouldn’t do is the product of often long political negotiations between countries and some of whom, such as China and the US or the EU and Russia, have severe geopolitical differences.
The ongoing discussion within ICCAT to strengthen the fins-attached rule is a prime example of how slow the decision-making process can be. Meant as a measure to stop sharks being caught at sea, definned and the carcasses thrown overboard, the present mechanism (an onboard fin-to-carcass ratio) is largely seen as inadequate. Proposals to change the rule so that all sharks caught must have the fins attached when landed are now in their 17th year of discussion at ICCAT, with no consensus in sight.
The FAO held a workshop in October 2025 for scientists working on blue shark fisheries. Several of the participants were associated with RFMOs. The workshop’s minutes indicate clearly that there are significant data problems. The minutes state “that across RFMOs there are widespread issues with both the quantity and quality of catch data… and with uncertainties in key biological parameters.”
The minutes further state: “Blue shark stocks are generally considered data poor, with limited composition data in many regions and catches frequently not reported at the species level (e.g. catches often aggregated as ‘shark’). Nominal catches are believed to be underreported, and estimates of unreported catch are often extrapolated based on limited data and broad assumptions.”
Frozen blue sharks landed at Kaohsiung fishing port, Taiwan. The port is a major base for Taiwan’s distant-water fishing fleet, where frozen catches are unloaded, weighed and prepared for processing and export. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)Kanziding Fish Market, Keelung, Taiwan. The wholesale fish market comes alive after midnight, when freshly landed seafood from Taiwan’s fishing fleets is auctioned and traded. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)Sharks at Kanziding Fish Market in Keelung, Taiwan. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)
Given the lack of data, how then do RFMOs declare that blue shark fishing is sustainable? What does happen is that RFMO scientific committees provide probabilistic assessments for the state of the stock. ICCAT held a crucial meeting in November 2025 where 54 countries met to decide upon the fate of tuna, blue sharks and other species in the Atlantic.
The scientific committee noted that 93% of total accumulated shark catches were blue sharks. Based upon a stock assessment done in 2023, the committee stated in 2025 that North Atlantic blue sharks had “50.1% probability of being overfished”. For the South Atlantic, the committee states that there is a “54.5% probability of overfishing”.
These probabilities are sufficient for ICCAT to declare the blue shark fishery sustainable.
But to take a 50% bet on one’s pension, the children’s university fund or the mortgage would be highly unwise. Yet this is what ICCAT is doing. Throwing the dice and hoping for even.
As Daniel Pauly says of the probability: “People that are willing to accept 50% are not guided by science.”
Iris Ziegler represents Deutsche Stiftung Meeresschutz, an NGO that has observer status at both ICCAT and the RFMO for the Indian Ocean. She’s a scientist and, in terms of being safe from overfishing, she says: “I would really want to see a higher probability for sharks – ideally at least 70% probability and having such a probability both in the near future and in the longer-term perspective.”
Luis Gustavo Cardoso is the vice-chair of ICCAT’s scientific committee. In response to Daily Maverick’s query about whether the 50% probability threshold was scientifically rigorous, his written reply was: “A framework calibrated only to very high certainty thresholds would systematically under-use a renewable resource capable of meeting food security needs sustainably – so the 50% convention for describing current status, combined with the precautionary buffers applied in forward-looking catch advice, is the balance the science is designed to strike.”
For the Mediterranean, where blue sharks are caught as bycatch, Ziegler would like to ban fleets from retaining the sharks. The sharks would have to be returned to the sea alive. There would also have to be, in her view, strict controls to reduce bycatch mortality.
Ziegler also states that there needs to be a “quota for blue sharks for the fishing nations in all ocean basins” and the setting of total allowable catch limits for each fishery. The Indian Ocean, which is administered by the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission (IOTC), is an example of how far away that goal remains. Blue sharks fall under the IOTC’s mandate.
A 2025 IOTC scientific assessment of the stock states that “maintaining current catches is likely to result in decreasing biomass and the stock becoming overfished and subject to overfishing in the near future”. The assessment also notes that there are no “harvest control rules for any shark species”.
Frozen sharks landed by Taiwan’s distant-water longline fleet after fishing trips lasting up to three months. These vessels target sharks, which are landed with their fins and carcasses retained for processing. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)Sharks landed as bycatch on the auction floor at Nanfangao fishing port. Taiwan requires sharks to be landed with their fins naturally attached, prohibiting the removal of fins at sea. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)
At an IOTC meeting in 2026 to discuss the stock status, only one country put forth a proposal in regards to catch limits. Japan’s proposal was to postpone the entire discussion on blue shark catch limits and to remove a bycatch mortality prevention measure. Accordingly, no quota was set.
In other words, the countries of the IOTC chose not to act upon the advice of IOTC scientists to limit blue shark catches even in the face of looming overfishing.
In the North Pacific and based upon a 2022 stock assessment, the probability of not being overfished is 62%. New assessments are planned for the North and Southwest Pacific in 2027. According to the FAO, both of their current stock assessments suffer from data issues and uncertainty.
Interestingly, the FAO also states that in the Southwest Pacific the “highest catches (by numbers) occur around New Zealand and Tasmania, where most landings are juveniles and small individuals”.
There has yet to be a stock assessment for the Southeastern Pacific.
The Pew Charitable Trusts is another accredited NGO observer at ICCAT and the Pew’s lead at ICCAT is Esther Wozniak. She’s been attending official ICCAT meetings for the past seven years. Of the probability factor, she’s in agreement with Ziegler and would like a 70% probability of not being overfished.
Despite probabilities being lower than 70% in key blue shark fisheries, Wozniak is not in favour of instituting quotas across all blue shark fisheries at the moment, stating that quotas have to be a “science-based process. Because if we as an organisation just go and tell them [RFMOs] you have to close the fishery, it’s not going to be very well received… they want the recommendation itself to come from their own scientists.”
Asked about the independence of the scientists at RFMOs, Pauly says “they are not independent. Most of them are hacks that are put there by the countries [to] enable them to have a high quota. The RFMOs don’t contribute much to rebuilding any stock and they contribute to the overall fishing scene.”
He adds: “Essentially my view of fisheries is that any fishery is potentially committing suicide. It’s like a guy running around with a knife and you have to prevent [him] from stabbing himself.”
The Indian Ocean Tuna Commission and the Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission did not respond to Daily Maverick’s queries regarding the sustainability of their blue shark fisheries.
Small sharks sold at Daxi fishing port, where freshly landed fish are traded locally. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)
The Pew Charitable Trusts engages with the General Fisheries Commission for the Mediterranean (GFCM). On the proposition that there should be a quota for blue sharks in the Mediterranean, Wozniak says: “I think GFCM as a body under FAO has done a good job of increasing their overall assessment and trying to figure out which species are in decline and which species are doing better. And I think there’s more work to be done on blue sharks there.”
The General Fisheries Commission for the Mediterranean recently published The State of Mediterranean and Black Sea Fisheries 2025. Out of 204 pages, blue sharks are mentioned only three times. The report labels blue shark catches as ‘incidental’ or cases of bycatch and declares that blue sharks are exposed to “fishing pressure”.
But the science on the Mediterranean is in and there is no doubt. The IUCN is an independent scientific organisation and is free from the control of fishing nations. It is charged with determining which species are heading towards extinction and it clearly states that the blue shark “population in the Mediterranean is declining at a critical rate and exists in an extremely depleted state”.
In fact, the research findings have been there for years so there is no excuse not to advocate for and implement drastic measures. Along with two other authors, Pauly wrote in a 2019 paper on the Mediterranean: “Following centuries of exploitation and the more recent expansion and intensification of fisheries, elasmobranchs [sharks, rays and swordfish] have become increasingly rare, with precipitous population declines.”
One cannot conserve a species by continuing to kill vast numbers of that species.
The General Fisheries Commission for the Mediterranean did not reply to Daily Maverick’s queries concerning blue shark conservation measures.
Since, and by common agreement, the blue shark fisheries are data poor, there is an urgent need to rectify the situation. According to both the FAO and the scientific committees of the various RFMOs, there is a better system of monitoring blue shark stocks than doing a stock assessment and having a political negotiation. A better system that isn’t being implemented, confounded with country disagreements.
Blue sharks are winched up in bunches from boats at the Taiwanese port of Donggang, a four-hour drive from Taipei. The fins are attached to the bodies, as per Taiwanese regulations. The sharks are put down on the concrete pier, small front-end loaders collect the bodies and place them in refrigerated trucks.
While the whole process is fast and well practised, the sharks aren’t the star of the show. That’s yellowfin tuna, a far more valuable fish than the sharks, and there’s a row of restaurants right next to the pier selling tuna sashimi. As with swordfish, blue sharks are caught alongside yellowfin tuna.
Prices at Donggang for blue shark meat are between R10 and 13/kg. Fins go for R240/kg. The North Pacific is where Taiwan fishes the hardest for blue sharks: Taiwan caught 26,462 tonnes in 2024 – its record catch for 2009-2024.
Fishing vessels in Nanfangao, Taiwan's second-largest fishing port. Many of the distant-water longliners based here spend around three months in the Pacific targeting tuna and swordfish before returning to unload their catch. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)
A relatively new method for assessing the health of a fishery, one that is used in some tuna fisheries, has a name that will get a bureaucrat excited: a management strategy evaluation. As is inevitable in the technical world of fisheries management, there’s an initialism, MSE.
An MSE is a dynamic process where data from a fishery is compared to a series of objective parameters. The parameters could be female-male ratio of catches, size of individuals caught, the level of fishing, catch maximisation or something else. If the data indicates that the parameters are breached, corrective measures such as bans on fishing at certain times of the year or decreasing the quota kick in. Countries don’t negotiate the corrective measures, the MSE institutes them.
The FAO is fully supportive of MSEs for blue sharks. Asked what would happen if MSEs weren’t implemented, Wozniak says: “I think it will be a very bleak future for the blue sharks.”
At this juncture, a note of caution. An MSE isn’t a magic wand that will restore blue shark populations or replace the lack of data.
Kwang-Ming Liu retired from his position as professor of marine affairs and resource management at the National Taiwan Ocean University in 2025. He says of the MSE: “I don’t think this management measure can be applied for data-limited shark species in the Pacific now. A precautionary catch quota for certain species may be a more practical approach.”
A shop on Taipei’s historic Dihua Street displays dried shark fins alongside sea cucumbers and other traditional delicacies. For more than a century, the neighbourhood has been one of Taiwan’s main centres for the wholesale trade in dried foods. Dried shark fins on sale ranged from about €280 to nearly €700. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams) A shop on Taipei’s historic Dihua Street displays dried shark fins alongside sea cucumbers and other traditional delicacies. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)
Liu also points to the need for a broader conservation measure: “A reduction of fishing effort for tuna fishery may ensure the sustainability of tuna species and the bycatch (sharks).”
Unlike in the Pacific, the Atlantic fisheries have quotas and ICCAT has been trying to implement an MSE since at least 2024. However, the MSE’s objectives still haven’t been set for the Atlantic. At this year’s critical ICCAT meeting in April, the European Union’s proposal on objectives couldn’t find consensus. Even more broadly, there were disagreements about the nature of the MSE.
ICCAT is not an entirely transparent organisation and minutes of its meetings don’t name the countries involved. Instead, countries are blandly called CPCs and hiding behind an initialism, it could be said, is a way to avoid public disclosure.
From the minutes of the April 2026 meeting, we do know that one country wanted to prioritise an MSE for short-fin mako over blue sharks, with the reasoning that the MSE for short-fin mako was already delayed. Others wanted to do both species together. Another wanted to do the blue shark MSE before the one for short-fin mako. Several were concerned about the number of MSEs being conducted.
The upshot is that the discussion ended without consensus and no blue shark MSE objectives were set. Further discussions are slated for an ICCAT meeting in November 2026.
The danger is that lack of agreement causes delays in implementation. ICCAT’s own internal documentation states that delays increase “the risk of the 2023 assessment data becoming outdated. If the MSE is postponed significantly, the cost of reconditioning models or restarting after a new assessment becomes unavoidable, effectively resetting the process.”
Shark loins are cut for export to Spain, Italy, France, Morocco and Brazil. The remainder is diced by hand for ready meals, canteens and paella mixes. The meat fetches €1.50 to €1.80 a kilo, the fins €15. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams) Processed blue shark is held at -25°C before it becomes steaks and paella mix. Tuna, the company’s most valuable product, is stored separately at -50°C. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)The skin is removed and exported to China, where it is used for leather products. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)
According to Zeigler, the next ICCAT stock assessment should be in 2028. If there are delays in the MSE implementation or an MSE doesn’t happen by then, the countries at ICCAT will begin a round of political negotiations over the 2028 stock assessment.
In effect, preventing the MSE for blue sharks is achievable simply by delaying the MSE’s implementation.
The eminent fisheries scientist John Gulland comes to mind at this point. He once said: “Fisheries management is an interminable debate about the condition of fish stocks until all doubt is removed. And so are all the fish.”
The skin is removed. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)Sharks with fins removed after landing. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)A shark caught as bycatch lies on the quay at Nanfangao fishing port before being auctioned. Under Taiwanese law, sharks must be landed with their fins naturally attached, prohibiting finning at sea. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)
The Kanziding fish market in Keelung, a port city in Taiwan’s north, only starts at one in the morning. Vendors set up their wares at the sides of the downtown streets and people fill the roads, browsing and shopping. The variety of marine species is staggering. Blue-spotted parrotfish, squid, pacific cutlassfish, frozen Norwegian salmon, yellowfin tuna and so many others – a veritable undergraduate degree in marine biology. Here and there you find blue sharks.
A customer speaks to a vendor who then places a blue shark, sans head or fins, down on the washed concrete floor. The fishmonger carefully examines the carcass, figuring out the ideal cut. The customer walks away with a fair bit of shark in a transparent bag. In Taiwan, fish markets have an honesty often not found in the West. Marine products aren’t sanitised in supermarket vacuum packs, processed into anonymised cubes and loins. You see exactly what you are buying in Taiwan and markets like Kanziding are the end points of the blue shark value chain.
Blue shark meat at Kanziding goes for R126/kg and in wealthy and expensive Taiwan that’s a bargain. Fins aren’t sold at Kanziding. Instead, they’re at stores specialising in ingredients for high-end cooking and Chinese traditional medicine. Top-quality blue shark fins can go up to R20,000 a kilo.
Chin-chang Wu pours green tea and has an old-school politeness about him. Blue shark fins are in a glass cabinet to the side of his desk and a little bit further, closer to the entrance, there’s a bag of dried blue shark skin. Seventy years ago, Wu’s father opened the store, which is in the southern city of Kaohsiung.
Retailer Chin-chang Wu, who sells shark products in Taipei, says he will continue as long as the trade is legal. (Photo: Tristen Taylor)
Shark fins are no longer the sales item they used to be and he has no new stock. Wu says: “Young people now eat less shark fin. Young people aren’t like the older generation, who liked eating shark fin. That’s gone now. So demand has fallen. That’s the first thing. Second, when their parents want to buy shark fin, young people will scold them.”
“This line of business,” Wu adds, “is gradually disappearing. The margin isn’t good.”
His biggest sellers are abalone, dried scallops, mushrooms and fish maw (swim bladder), and he’s adamant that his business isn’t dependent on fins. If customers want fins and the trade remains legal, he’ll sell fins. If he can’t sell, either from dropped demand or changes in the law, his store will go on just fine.
Asked about a quota for shark fishing, Wu says that “if shark output keeps falling, I support it, protecting sharks. If the scientists, the professionals, think sharks have declined, then I think reducing it is reasonable.”
The large red Chinese characters behind his desk translate to integrity.
Only after landing are the fins removed. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams) Workers unload the catch of one Pacific longliner, shipped frozen from Peru in five containers: about 130 tonnes of swordfish, 15 of blue shark. Ibáñez processes up to 6,000 tonnes of blue shark a year, caught in the Atlantic and the Pacific. The fins go to Asia, the meat to Europe, Morocco and Brazil. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams) One of ARVI’s recipe books promoting tintorera, the Spanish name for blue shark. Through cookbooks, cooking demonstrations and collaborations with local restaurants, the association encourages consumers to eat the species. (Photo: Nathalie Bertrams)
And this is where we are at. Decisions on quotas and harvest restrictions are being made on politics and on the basis of extremely limited data, broad assumptions and reckless probabilities. Despite IUCN warnings, a CITES listing and the collapse of the entire Mediterranean shark fishery, RFMOs and nation states are acting as if blue sharks are an inexhaustible resource. The absurdity of refusing to implement precautionary quotas extends all the way down to a civil society organisation embedded within the RFMO for the Atlantic.
The world is eating way more fish than it used to. In 1950, the global average per capita consumption of fish was an estimated 6.5kg. Annual per capita consumption in 2023 was about 21.1kg. Over the same period the world’s population grew from about 2.5 billion to eight billion.
The only way this situation is possible is to fish hard. To exploit every resource, in every sea and ocean. An unrelenting assault hurling sharks towards extinction. DM

东盟与中国未能敲定南海行为准则 |中国劳工公告栏
星期一, 16 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
东盟与中国未能敲定南海行为准则
在菲律宾主持下，东盟与中国之间关于拖延已久的南海行为准则的谈判未能达成协议。菲律宾外交部长马。特蕾莎·拉扎罗表示，几个关键问题仍未解决，包括该准则是否具有法律约束力。
马尼拉外交部长周日表示，尽管就草案的约 80% 达成了临时协议，但东盟和中国未能在菲律宾主持下完成拖延已久的南海行为准则谈判。
东盟-中国南海行为准则的谈判已经拖延了二十多年，但作为现任主席国的菲律宾承诺加快谈判速度，并在今年完成准则。
“目前还没有结论，”菲律宾外长马说。特里萨·拉扎罗 (Theresa Lazaro) 在马尼拉举行的东南亚国家联盟 (ASEAN) 11 国峰会新闻发布会上表示，一些关键问题仍未解决，包括该准则是否具有法律约束力的问题。 “东盟国家和中国对事情的真相也有不同的看法，”她补充道。
中国的东南亚邻国希望该准则以国际法为基础，他们一再指责北京在宣称对几乎整个南海拥有主权时无视国际法。北京坚称其在南海的行动合法且专业。
中国广泛的海事主张与文莱、印度尼西亚、马来西亚、菲律宾和越南的专属经济区重叠，这使得制定功能性法规对于防止紧张局势升级和管理海上事件至关重要。 2016年，一个国际仲裁庭裁定，中国的全面主张没有国际法依据，但北京方面拒绝接受这一裁决。
近年来，马尼拉和北京陷入了一系列海上对抗，菲律宾指责中国在其专属经济区内一再采取侵略行动，包括危险的演习、高压水炮和扰乱补给任务。中国则指责菲律宾侵犯其声称的领土。
分析人士表示，分歧不仅仅存在于东盟和中国之间。新加坡拉惹勒南国际研究学院高级研究员科林·许(Collin Koh)表示，东盟成员国之间的分歧，包括在该准则的地理范围上的分歧，也减慢了谈判速度。 “除了北京之外，东盟内部的分歧也发挥着重要作用，”他说。 Koh表示，剩余的分歧将很难解决，需要各方做出“重大让步”。新加坡明年担任东盟轮值主席国时，将继承努力就行为准则达成一致的任务。

ASEAN, China fail to finalise South China Sea code of conduct
Negotiations on a long-delayed South China Sea code of conduct between ASEAN and China concluded without agreement under the Philippines' chairmanship. Philippine Foreign Minister Ma. Theresa Lazaro said several key issues remain unresolved, including whether the code would be legally binding.
ASEAN and China were unable to conclude negotiations on a long-delayed South China Sea code of conduct under the Philippines' chairmanship, despite reaching provisional agreement on about 80 per cent of the draft, Manila's foreign minister said on Sunday.
Negotiations on an ASEAN-China Code of Conduct in the South China Sea have dragged on for over two decades, but the Philippines, as current chair, had committed to speed up those talks and conclude the code this year.
“There is no conclusion yet,” Philippine foreign minister Ma. Theresa Lazaro told a press conference at a summit of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations in Manila, adding that several key issues remain unresolved, including questions over whether the code would be legally binding. “The ASEAN countries plus China have also different views on how things are,” she added.
China's Southeast Asian neighbours want the code to be grounded in international law, which they have repeatedly accused Beijing of disregarding as it asserts its sovereignty over nearly all of the South China Sea. Beijing maintains that its actions in the South China Sea have been lawful and professional.
China's extensive maritime claims overlap with the exclusive economic zones of Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam, making a functional code essential to preventing any escalation of tensions and managing incidents at sea. An international arbitration tribunal ruled in 2016 that China's sweeping claims have no basis under international law, a decision that Beijing rejects.
Manila and Beijing have been locked in a series of maritime confrontations in recent years, with the Philippines accusing China of repeated aggressive actions inside its exclusive economic zone, including dangerous manoeuvres, water-cannoning and disrupting resupply missions. China, for its part, has accused the Philippines of intruding into what it claims as its territory.
Analysts say the disagreements are not only between ASEAN and China. Collin Koh, a senior fellow at Singapore's S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies, said divisions among ASEAN members, including over the geographical scope of the code, had also slowed negotiations. “Other than Beijing, intramural divergences within ASEAN also play a significant role,” he said. Koh said the remaining differences would be difficult to resolve and would require “major concessions” from the various parties. Singapore will inherit the task of trying to secure agreement on the code of conduct when it assumes the ASEAN chairmanship next year.

香港海洋公园珊瑚展览吸引百万游客 |中国劳工公告栏
星期一, 16 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
香港海洋公园珊瑚展览吸引百万游客
环境及自然保育基金拨款超过350万港元，在海洋公园大水族馆举办的珊瑚修复展览吸引了超过一百万名参观者。该倡议将康复与公共教育结合起来，以 12 种本土珊瑚物种为特色，并在
香港正加紧努力，通过珊瑚修复和公众教育活动来保护海洋生物多样性。据《The Standard》报道，在海洋公园的大水族馆，由环境及自然保育基金（ECF）支持的专门珊瑚展览已吸引了超过一百万名游客。
该展览获环保基金资助逾350万港元，展示了12种原产于当地水域的硬珊瑚和软珊瑚品种。该展览既是一个康复场地，也是一个生活教室。这笔资金还用于翻新其他水族馆设施以及建立珊瑚生态和保护探索中心，该中心现在是珊瑚恢复和公共教育的重要场所。
该倡议依赖于协作框架。香港中文大学从当地水域收集珊瑚碎片并提供科学专业知识，而海洋公园则提供优质的护理设施。健康的人工养殖碎片最终将被移植回香港南部水域，以重建枯竭的珊瑚群落。
作为展览的补充，珊瑚生态和保护探索中心为学生和公众举办沉浸式 STEAM 研讨会。该中心旨在提高人们对海洋保护和珊瑚生态系统重要性的认识。
环保基金委员会主席郑锦忠指出，该基金在32年里已向超过7,200个环保项目分配超过47亿港元。他表示，该基金将引导未来努力实现本地绿色转型和《2050年香港气候行动计划》。

Ocean Park coral exhibition draws one million visitors in Hong Kong
A coral restoration exhibition at Ocean Park's Grand Aquarium, backed by over HK$3.5 million from the Environment and Conservation Fund, has attracted more than one million visitors. The initiative combines rehabilitation with public education, featuring 12 native coral species and workshops at the
Hong Kong is stepping up efforts to protect its marine biodiversity through coral restoration and public education initiatives. At Ocean Park's Grand Aquarium, a specialised coral exhibition backed by the Environment and Conservation Fund (ECF) has drawn over one million visitors, according to a report by The Standard.
Awarded more than HK$3.5 million from the ECF, the display showcases 12 hard and soft coral species native to local waters. The exhibition acts as both a rehabilitation ground and a living classroom. The funding also covered renovations to other aquarium facilities and the establishment of the Coral Ecology and Conservation Discovery Centre, now a key venue for coral rehabilitation and public education.
The initiative relies on a collaborative framework. The Chinese University of Hong Kong collects coral fragments from local waters and provides scientific expertise, while Ocean Park offers quality care facilities. Healthy, cultivated fragments will eventually be transplanted back into southern Hong Kong waters to rebuild depleted coral communities.
Complementing the exhibition, the Coral Ecology and Conservation Discovery Centre runs immersive STEAM workshops for students and the public. The centre aims to raise awareness about marine conservation and the importance of coral ecosystems.
ECF committee chairman Eric Cheng Kam-chung noted that the fund has distributed over HK$4.7 billion across more than 7,200 environmental projects over 32 years. He said the fund will steer future efforts toward local green transitions and the Hong Kong Climate Action Plan 2050.

英伟达财报、亚太经合组织峰会、美国零售销售将推动市场一周中国劳工公告栏
星期一, 16 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
英伟达财报、亚太经合组织峰会、美国零售销售将推动本周市场
首席执行官辞职后，英伟达周二公布第三季度财报； APEC工商领导人峰会周二在深圳开幕；美国零售销售数据将于周二公布；中国周一发布10月份经济数据；香港消费者价格指数将于周五到期。
据《标准报》报道，前首席执行官黄仁勋因婚外情被曝光而辞职，截至周五，英伟达市值从 1.9 万亿美元增至 3.9 万亿美元，该公司将于周二公布第三季度财报。根据 LSEG 的数据，分析师预测这家芯片巨头第三财季的营收将达到 1090 亿美元（8502 亿港元），盈利增长将达到 90%。
一批中国科技巨头将在未来一周发布最新业绩，包括腾讯、百度、阿里巴巴、京东、快手科技、网易和联想。
亚太经合组织（APEC）经济体的 12 位领导人将出席定于周二至周三在深圳举行的 2026 年 APEC 工商领导人峰会。中国国家主席习近平将与澳大利亚、加拿大、智利、中国香港、印度尼西亚、韩国、马来西亚、墨西哥、俄罗斯、泰国和越南的领导人一起出席峰会。 115家世界500强企业的代表也将参加。 APEC领导人非正式会议定于周三和周四举行。
周二的美国零售销售数据将成为市场关注的焦点。该数据将让我们了解通胀是否仍在加剧，从而可能为美联储加息铺平道路。 10 月份美国消费者价格涨幅超出预期，上涨 0.4%，导致投资者押注美联储在未来几个月进一步加息。
中国将于周一公布10月份工业产出、零售销售、固定资产投资数据和失业率。市场预计，10月份中国工业产出增速将从上月的5.5%放缓至5.3%，而零售销售预计将增长0.8%，而9月份的增幅为1.1%。
香港10月份消费者物价指数数据将于周五公布，一个月前上涨1.9%。

Monday, 16 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Nvidia earnings, APEC summit, US retail sales to drive markets week
Nvidia reports Q3 earnings Tuesday after CEO resignation; APEC CEO Summit starts Tuesday in Shenzhen; US retail sales data due Tuesday; China releases October economic data Monday; Hong Kong CPI due Friday.
Nvidia will report its third-quarter earnings on Tuesday, after its market capitalisation swung from US$1.9 trillion to US$3.9 trillion as of Friday, following the resignation of former chief executive Jensen Huang amid revelations of extramarital affairs, according to The Standard. Analysts forecast the chip giant's earnings growth will reach 90 per cent on revenue of US$109 billion (HK$850.2 billion) for the company's fiscal third quarter, based on LSEG data.
A batch of Chinese tech giants will release their latest results in the coming week, including Tencent, Baidu, Alibaba, JD.com, Kuaishou Technology, NetEase and Lenovo.
Twelve leaders of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) economies will attend the APEC CEO Summit 2026, scheduled for Tuesday to Wednesday in Shenzhen. Chinese President Xi Jinping, along with leaders from Australia, Canada, Chile, China's Hong Kong, Indonesia, the Republic of Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, Russia, Thailand and Vietnam, will attend the summit. Representatives from 115 Fortune Global 500 companies will also participate. The APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting is set for Wednesday and Thursday.
Tuesday's US retail sales figures will be the focus for the market. The data will offer a read on whether inflation is still building, potentially paving the way for the Federal Reserve to hike rates. US consumer prices grew more than forecast in October, up 0.4 per cent, leading investors to bet on further Fed rate hikes in coming months.
China will release October industrial output, retail sales, fixed asset investment data and the unemployment rate on Monday. The market estimated that China's industrial output in October will slow from the 5.5 per cent increase recorded a month prior to 5.3 per cent, while retail sales are expected to log a 0.8 per cent growth in October, compared with the 1.1 per cent increase in September.
Hong Kong consumer price index figures for October will be released on Friday, after logging a 1.9 per cent rise a month ago.

summary: 眼科医生警告高度近视会使视网膜脱离风险增加39倍中国劳工公告2026年11月16日星期一·香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 眼科医生警告高度近视会使视网膜脱离风险增加39倍 香港眼科医生敦促定期进行眼科检查，警告超过600度的高度近视会使视网膜脱离风险增加39倍。 50 岁以下的病例增长最快。专家建议立即关注突然出现的飞蚊症或闪光，并对 40 岁以上的人进行年度散瞳检查。香港眼科医生呼吁公众
content:
眼科医生警告高度近视会使视网膜脱离风险增加39倍中国劳工公告栏
星期一, 16 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
眼科医生警告高度近视会使视网膜脱离风险增加39倍
香港眼科医生敦促定期进行眼科检查，警告超过600度的高度近视会使视网膜脱离的风险增加39倍。 50 岁以下的病例增长最快。专家建议立即关注突然出现的飞蚊症或闪光，并对 40 岁以上的人进行年度散瞳检查。
香港眼科医生呼吁公众定期进行眼部检查，发现警告信号时立即就医，并警告说，高度近视超过600度的人，视网膜脱离的风险可能是非近视者的39倍。
该警告是在 11 月 15 日由香港眼科医师学会、香港眼科学会和香港私家眼科医生协会联合举办的活动中发出的。为约100名18岁至70岁、近视600度及以上的公民提供免费眼底检查。
香港眼科学会主席任卓声在活动上致辞时表示，香港是全球儿童近视率最高的国家之一，自疫情爆发以来，这一趋势更加恶化。他解释说，随着近视恶化，眼球会变长，视网膜会变薄，从而增加流泪和脱离的风险。屈光手术无法逆转这些结构变化。任补充说，9岁或10岁的儿童就已被诊断出视网膜脱离，这凸显了早期干预的重要性。
香港眼科医学院院长容汉华解释说，普通的飞蚊症——眼睛玻璃体老化时出现的斑点或线条——通常对健康影响不大。但视野中飞蚊症突然增加、闪光或黑影可能预示着视网膜撕裂或脱离。他说治疗可能需要在几天内开始，延误可能会导致永久性视力丧失或失明。
香港眼科医学院理事会成员黎晓平表示，全球范围内视网膜脱离的病例正在增加，其中50岁以下人群的病例增长速度快于整体增长率。他援引研究表明，100至300度的近视会使视网膜脱离的风险增加四倍，而近视超过600度则使视网膜脱离的风险增加多达39倍。其他危险因素包括既往眼外伤、视网膜脱离家族史和视网膜脱离史。
专家建议，飞蚊症或闪光突然增加的人应立即就医。他们还建议40岁以上的人每年进行一次散瞳检查。

Ophthalmologists warn high myopia raises retinal detachment risk 39-fold | China Labour Bulletin Board
Monday, 16 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Ophthalmologists warn high myopia raises retinal detachment risk 39-fold
Hong Kong ophthalmologists urge regular eye exams, warning that high myopia exceeding 600 degrees increases retinal detachment risk up to 39 times. Cases among under-50s are rising fastest. Experts advise immediate attention for sudden floaters or flashes, and annual dilated exams for over-40s.
Ophthalmologists in Hong Kong have urged the public to undergo regular eye examinations and seek prompt medical attention for warning signs, warning that people with high myopia of more than 600 degrees may face up to 39 times the risk of retinal detachment compared with those without myopia.
The warning came during a joint event on 15 November organised by the College of Ophthalmologists of Hong Kong, the Hong Kong Ophthalmological Society and the Hong Kong Association of Private Eye Surgeons. Free fundus examinations were offered to about 100 citizens aged 18 to 70 with myopia of 600 degrees or higher.
Speaking at the event, Hong Kong Ophthalmological Society chairman Jason Yam Cheuk-sing said Hong Kong has one of the world's highest rates of childhood myopia, and the trend has worsened since the pandemic. He explained that as myopia worsens, the eyeball elongates and the retina becomes thinner, increasing the risk of tears and detachment. Refractive surgery cannot reverse these structural changes. Yam added that retinal detachment has been diagnosed in children as young as nine or 10, highlighting the importance of early intervention.
President of the College of Ophthalmologists of Hong Kong Yung Hon-wah explained that ordinary floaters — spots or lines that can appear as the vitreous in the eye ages — often have little effect on health. But a sudden increase in floaters, flashes of light or dark shadows in the field of vision may signal a retinal tear or detachment. He said treatment may need to begin within days and delays can lead to permanent vision loss or blindness.
Frank Lai Hiu-ping, a council member of the College of Ophthalmologists of Hong Kong, said cases of retinal detachment are increasing worldwide, with cases among people under 50 rising faster than the overall rate. He cited research that myopia of 100 to 300 degrees is associated with a fourfold increase in the risk of retinal detachment, while myopia exceeding 600 degrees raises the risk by up to 39 times. Other risk factors include previous eye injuries, a family history of retinal detachment and a prior detachment.
Experts advise people who experience a sudden increase in floaters or flashes of light to seek immediate medical attention. They also recommend that people over 40 have a dilated eye examination every year.

title: US minerals push lags as Trump meets Xi, leaving leverage with China
zh_title: 特朗普与习近平会面，美国矿产开发滞后，将影响力留给中国
summary: 特朗普与习近平会面，美国矿产开发滞后，将影响力留给中国中国劳工布告栏 周一，2026 年 11 月 16 日·香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 在特朗普与习近平会面时，美国矿产项目进展滞后，对中国留下了影响力 在与习近平会谈之前，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普确保国内关键矿产的战略仍未完成，大多数项目距离投产还有数年时间。分析人士表示，这使得美国制造商依赖中国材料，从而让北京在贸易谈判中发挥影响力。美国总统唐纳德·特朗普会见中国国家主席习近平
content:
特朗普与习近平会面，美国矿产开发滞后，将影响力留给中国中国劳工公告栏
星期一, 16 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
特朗普与习近平会面，美国矿产开发滞后，将影响力留给中国
在与习近平会谈之前，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普确保国内关键矿产的战略尚未完成，大多数项目距离投产还有数年时间。分析人士表示，这使得美国制造商依赖中国材料，从而让北京在贸易谈判中发挥影响力。
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普本周会见中国国家主席习近平，其贸易战略的一个关键部分尚未完成：确保关键矿产的本土供应，以对抗北京的主导地位。尽管联邦投资数十亿美元，许多美国采矿项目仍需数年时间才能投产，这使得美国制造商依赖于半导体、机器人、武器系统和人工智能繁荣所必需的中国材料。
这种依赖使特朗普在贸易谈判中处于尴尬的境地。路透社采访的六位分析师表示，他只能在关税和出口管制方面向习近平施加一定程度的压力，而不会冒着获得美国产量不足的金属、磁铁和化合物的风险。习近平利用中国作为世界最大稀土矿产国的地位作为筹码。去年，北京限制了矿物和磁铁的出口，扰乱了福特汽车和其他美国制造商的工作。华盛顿就继续访问进行了谈判。
总部位于华盛顿的商业咨询公司沃格尔集团(Vogel Group)贸易主管萨米尔·卡帕迪亚(Samir Kapadia)表示，特朗普的矿产野心与缓慢的执行速度之间的差距反映了重建美国在20世纪末几乎放弃的行业的难度。卡帕迪亚说：“目前 PowerPoint 的数量超出了允许的范围，因此问题是这些项目中有多少仅以 PDF 形式存在，有多少已经准备就绪。”白宫没有回应置评请求。
预计周四与习近平的会面将考验特朗普的战略。特朗普和习近平可能同意延长现有的贸易休战协议，该休战协议将于一月份到期，其中包括对某些关键矿产的出口管制豁免。美国国家矿业协会贸易小组负责人里奇·诺兰表示，中国人一直在对美国使用关键的矿物扼流圈。中国表示限制这些矿物是为了防止它们在战争中使用。它还指责华盛顿滥用出口管制，阻止向中国出口半导体。
与此同时，美国的生产却落后了。据国际能源署称，到 2025 年，其用于电动汽车和军事设备的钕铁硼磁铁的年产量约为 4,500 吨。而中国的年产量约为 210,000 吨。除了采矿业之外，中国还花费了数十年的时间建设将原材料转化为工业零部件所需的加工和精炼设施、技术专长和制造基础设施。 '我们现在在哪里？技术金属研究公司分析师杰克·利夫顿(Jack Lifton)表示，这正是中国人想要的：搞砸了，令人难以置信。
尽管特朗普政府已采取行动加速矿产项目，但大部分基础设施仍需数年时间才能建成，矿山、炼油厂和加工设施需要十年或更长时间才能投入使用。 7.4 美元一元

US minerals push lags as Trump meets Xi, leaving leverage with China | China Labour Bulletin Board
Monday, 16 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
US minerals push lags as Trump meets Xi, leaving leverage with China
Ahead of talks with Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump's strategy to secure domestic critical minerals remains unfinished, with most projects years from production. Analysts say this leaves American manufacturers dependent on Chinese materials, giving Beijing leverage in trade negotiations.
US President Donald Trump meets Chinese President Xi Jinping this week with a key part of his trade strategy unfinished: securing a homegrown supply of critical minerals to counter Beijing's dominance. Many US mining projects remain years from production despite billions of dollars in federal investment, leaving American manufacturers dependent on Chinese materials essential to semiconductors, robotics, weapons systems and the artificial intelligence boom.
That dependence puts Trump in an awkward position for trade talks. He can press Xi only so hard on tariffs and export controls without risking access to metals, magnets and chemical compounds that the US does not produce in sufficient quantities, according to half a dozen analysts interviewed by Reuters. Xi has used China's position as the world's top rare earths miner as leverage. Last year, Beijing restricted exports of the minerals and magnets, disrupting work at Ford Motor and other US manufacturers. Washington negotiated for continued access.
The gap between Trump's minerals ambitions and the slow pace of execution reflects the difficulty of rebuilding an industry the US nearly abandoned at the end of the 20th century, said Samir Kapadia, head of trade at the Washington-based business advisory firm Vogel Group. 'Right now there are more PowerPoint decks than permits, so the question is how many of these projects exist only in PDF form and how many are shovel-ready,' Kapadia said. The White House did not respond to a request for comment.
The meeting with Xi, expected on Thursday, will test Trump's strategy. Trump and Xi may agree to extend their existing trade truce, which is due to expire in January and includes export-control waivers for certain critical minerals. 'The Chinese have been using the critical minerals choke collar on the US when they feel like it,' said Rich Nolan, head of the National Mining Association trade group. China has said it restricted the minerals to prevent their use in war. It has also accused Washington of abusing export controls by blocking semiconductor exports to China.
Meanwhile, the US has lagged in production. Its manufacturing capacity for neodymium-iron-boron magnets, used in electric vehicles and military equipment, was roughly 4,500 metric tons annually in 2025. That compared with about 210,000 metric tons in China, according to the International Energy Agency. Beyond mining, China has spent decades building the processing and refining facilities, technical expertise and manufacturing infrastructure needed to turn raw materials into industrial components. 'Where are we now? Exactly where the Chinese want us: screwed up beyond belief,' said Jack Lifton, an analyst with Technology Metals Research.
While the Trump administration has moved to accelerate mineral projects, much of the infrastructure remains years away, with mines, refineries and processing facilities requiring a decade or more to come online. A US$7.4 billion Tennessee refinery for copper, zinc and other critical minerals backed by South Korea's Korea Zinc is not expected to open until 2030. Rio Tinto and BHP aim to build North America's largest copper mine, but it would not open until next decade. Last year, Trump's administration agreed to take an equity stake in Trilogy Metals, which plans to produce copper in Alaska starting in 2031. Vulcan Elements has begun making rare earth magnets in North Carolina, although its customers have not yet approved them for use. Some projects are further along: MP Materials is expanding magnet production in Texas under a multibillion-dollar Pentagon partnership, Nevada's Thacker Pass mine is under construction with production expected in 2028, and Perpetua Resources plans to produce antimony in Idaho by 2029.
Trump's minerals strategy also faces a political test at home. Democrats' midterm victories will give them control of Congress next year, and some have questioned the administration's investments in private companies. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright, whose department funded multiple minerals projects, said last week he is 'happy to explain everything we've done.'

title: Hong Kong’s new uncertificated securities market draws 2,700 listed firms
zh_title: 香港新的无证证券市场吸引2,700家上市公司
summary: 香港新的无证证券市场吸引2,700家上市公司|中国劳工布告栏 星期一, 16 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 香港新的无证证券市场吸引了 2,700 家上市公司 香港首个无证证券市场 (USM) 于周一生效，现有 2,700 家上市公司将在五年内进行整合。证券及期货事务监察委员会表示，实物股票仍然有效，市场提供无纸化灵活性。香港首个非认证证券市场（USM）于Monda生效
content:
香港新的无证证券市场吸引2,700家上市公司|中国劳工公告栏
星期一, 16 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
香港新的无证证券市场吸引2,700家上市公司
香港首个非认证证券市场 (USM) 于周一生效，预计将在五年内整合 2,700 家现有上市公司。证券及期货事务监察委员会表示，实物股票仍然有效，市场提供无纸化灵活性。
香港证券及期货事务监察委员会（证监会）宣布，香港首个非认证证券市场（USM）于周一生效，已有 2,700 家现有上市公司排队在五年过渡期内融入新系统。
证监会表示，USM 消除了手动和纸质流程的需要，为投资者提供了更多选择，提高了市场效率，并建立了更稳健的市场。
该委员会表示，从周一开始，现有的实物股票不会失效或自动转换为无纸化形式。发行人和市场将可以灵活地决定何时将其股票转换为无纸化形式，并且他们将收到这些安排的提前通知。
市场分析认为，新上市证券审批流程并未因该安排而发生实质性变化。发行人已将无纸化安排纳入上市流程，大部分已做好充分准备。
Computershare Hong Kong企业服务副总裁Ivy Ng表示，该制度将解决丢失实体证书的问题。股东只需像其他网络平台一样点击“忘记密码”或“忘记账户”功能，即可轻松管理其持股账户，例如重置登录账户或密码。他们不再需要办理登报报纸通知、挂失等手续来更换实物凭证。

Monday, 16 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong’s new uncertificated securities market draws 2,700 listed firms
Hong Kong’s first uncertificated securities market (USM) takes effect on Monday, with 2,700 existing listed companies set to integrate over five years. The Securities and Futures Commission says physical shares remain valid, and the market offers paperless flexibility.
Hong Kong’s first uncertificated securities market (USM) took effect on Monday, with 2,700 existing listed companies already lined up to integrate into the new system over a five-year transition period, the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) announced.
The USM eliminates the need for manual and paper-based processes, giving investors more choices, enhancing market efficiency, and establishing a more robust market, the SFC said.
The commission stated that existing physical share certificates will not become invalid or automatically convert into paperless form from Monday. Issuers and the market will have the flexibility to decide when to convert their shares into paperless form, and they will receive advance notice of these arrangements.
Market analysis indicates that the new listed securities approval process has not undergone substantive changes due to the arrangement. Issuers have incorporated paperless arrangements into the listing process, with most being well prepared.
Ivy Ng, vice president of corporate services at Computershare Hong Kong, said the regime will solve the problem of losing physical certificates. Shareholders can easily manage their shareholding accounts, such as resetting their login account or password, simply by clicking on the “forgot password” or “forgot account” functions like on other online platforms. They no longer need to go through procedures such as publishing newspaper notices or reporting loss to replace physical certificates.

港澳办主任夏宝龙听取深圳工作情况通报
周日，港澳事务办公室主任夏宝龙在深圳听取了有关工作情况的通报。该办公室没有透露具体议程项目或通报人的身份。
据港澳事务办公室官方网站报道，港澳事务办公室主任夏宝龙周日在深圳听取了“相关工作情况”通报。港澳办没有透露任何具体议程项目或通报人士的身份。
港澳办常务副主任、国务院港澳事务办公室徐其芳也出席。
去年12月1日，港澳办曾发布类似公告，称夏大埔宏福苑火灾后曾在深圳听取“有关情况”通报。

HKMAO chief Xia Baolong receives Shenzhen briefing on work situations
Xia Baolong, director of the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office, received a briefing on 'relevant work situations' in Shenzhen on Sunday. The office did not disclose specific agenda items or the identities of the briefers.
Xia Baolong, director of the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office (HKMAO), heard a briefing on “relevant work situations” in Shenzhen on Sunday, according to the office’s official website. The HKMAO did not disclose any specific agenda items or the identities of the individuals delivering the briefings.
The executive deputy director of the HKMAO and the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office of the State Council, Xu Qifang, was also in attendance.
On 1 December last year, the HKMAO previously issued a similar announcement stating that Xia had heard a briefing on “relevant situations” in Shenzhen, following the fire at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po.

summary: 人工智能产品出口带动香港40年来最快月度贸易增长中国劳工布告栏 星期一，2026 年 11 月 16 日·香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 人工智能产品出口推动香港实现 40 年来最快的月度贸易增长 据商务部长邱腾华称，香港 9 月份的出口同比飙升逾 60%，为四十多年来最快的单月增长。尽管丘警告说，香港的出口激增超过 7000 亿港元，但人工智能相关电子产品的繁荣推动了转口额超过 7000 亿港元。
content:
人工智能产品出口带动香港40年来最快月度贸易增长中国劳工公告栏
星期一, 16 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
人工智能产品出口带动香港40年来最快月度贸易增长
香港商务部长邱腾华表示，9 月份香港出口同比飙升逾 60%，是四十多年来最快的单月增长。尽管丘警告说，这一繁荣是由人工智能相关电子产品推动的，推动转口额超过 7000 亿港元
香港商务及经济发展局局长邱英华表示，9月份香港出口较去年同月飙升逾60%，创下40多年来最快的单月增速。
丘表示，快速增长主要是由人工智能相关电子产品的出口推动的。这一激增使香港每年的转口贸易额超过7000亿港元，相当于香港国内生产总值的1.4倍。
然而，丘警告称，尽管部分地区冲突可能出现缓和迹象，但全球前景仍存在高度不确定性，香港经济仍容易受到外围因素的影响。他指出，人工智能技术的快速扩张可能会放缓。
邱腾华表示，政府将继续密切关注全球趋势，探索新机遇，积极拓展香港的贸易网络​​。
丘还强调，亚太经合组织领导人非正式会议将于本周在深圳开幕，旨在促进区域经济合作、和平共同发展、贸易创新和人工智能进步。
此外，邱腾华指出，香港已获纳入区域全面经济伙伴关系协定的入世工作组，使香港能够游说个别成员国支持其加入该贸易协定。成功加入后，协议项下的各项贸易安排将自动延伸至香港，为香港经济带来实实在在的利益。

AI product exports drive Hong Kong's fastest monthly trade growth in 40 years | China Labour Bulletin Board
Monday, 16 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
AI product exports drive Hong Kong's fastest monthly trade growth in 40 years
Hong Kong's exports surged more than 60 per cent year-on-year in September, the fastest single-month growth in over four decades, according to Commerce Secretary Algernon Yau. The boom was driven by artificial-intelligence-related electronics, pushing re-exports past HK$700 billion, though Yau warne
Hong Kong's exports surged by more than 60 per cent in September compared with the same month last year, marking the fastest single-month growth rate in more than 40 years, according to Algernon Yau Ying-wah, Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development.
Yau said the rapid expansion was primarily driven by the export of artificial-intelligence-related electronic products. The surge has pushed the city's annual re-export trade value to more than HK$700 billion, equivalent to 1.4 times Hong Kong's gross domestic product.
However, Yau warned that the global outlook remains highly uncertain and Hong Kong's economy remains susceptible to external factors, even though some regional conflicts may show signs of easing. He noted that the rapid expansion of AI technology could potentially slow down.
The government will continue to closely monitor global trends, explore new opportunities, and actively expand the city's trade networks, Yau said.
Yau also highlighted that the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting is set to begin in Shenzhen this week, aiming to foster regional economic cooperation, peaceful co-development, trade innovation and AI advancement.
Furthermore, Yau noted that Hong Kong has been included in the Accession Working Group under the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, which enables Hong Kong to lobby individual member states in support of its bid to join the trade pact. Upon successful accession, the various trade arrangements under the agreement will automatically extend to Hong Kong, bringing substantial benefits to the local economy.

香港插画家在政府支持下上海童书展上展示作品 |中国劳工公告栏
星期一, 16 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
香港插画家获政府支持在上海童书展展示作品
香港文化创意产业办事处资助上海国际童书展香港馆，展出“飞天绘本”计划的插画家。本土插画家刘庆华入围金风车国际青年插画家大赛
香港特别行政区政府文化创意产业办公室资助于2026年11月15日开幕的上海国际童书展设立香港馆，展示第三届「飞翔绘本——香港绘本插画家参与国际书展推广计划」支持的插画家的作品。
继2026年4月参加意大利博洛尼亚童书展之后，该计划的八位插画家再次参展。上海童书展期间，插画家们展示作品、举办分享会、与出版商会面，探讨市场潜力和商机。
“飞行绘本”计划还资助选定的插画家创作新作品并参加国际绘本或插画比赛，以提高他们的全球知名度。本土插画家刘庆华凭借作品《座头鲸，回家吧！》在上海博览会上获得认可。晋级上海国际童书展主办的2026年金风车国际青年插画家大赛50强。本次大赛共吸引了来自73个国家和地区的2000余份参赛作品。
此外，香港馆亦展示第二版《飞天绘本》八位插画家的作品，以及文创局资助的「香港绘本出版支援计划」下出版的十四位香港及两位内地插画家的原创绘本。展览旨在向世界各地的出版商介绍优质的香港绘本。

Hong Kong illustrators showcase works at Shanghai children's book fair with government support | China Labour Bulletin Board
Monday, 16 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong illustrators showcase works at Shanghai children's book fair with government support
Hong Kong's Cultural and Creative Industries Office funded a Hong Kong pavilion at the Shanghai International Children's Book Fair, featuring illustrators from its "Flying Picture Books" scheme. Local illustrator Liu Qinghua was shortlisted in the Golden Windmill International Young Illustrators Con
The Cultural and Creative Industries Office of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government has funded a Hong Kong pavilion at the Shanghai International Children's Book Fair, which opened on 15 November 2026. The pavilion showcases the work of illustrators supported by the third edition of the 'Flying Picture Books – Hong Kong Picture Book Illustrators at International Book Fairs Promotion Scheme'.
Eight illustrators from the scheme are exhibiting at the fair, building on their participation at the Bologna Children's Book Fair in Italy in April 2026. During the Shanghai fair, the illustrators are displaying their works, holding sharing sessions, and meeting publishers to explore market potential and business opportunities.
The 'Flying Picture Books' scheme also funds selected illustrators to create new works and enter international picture book or illustration competitions to raise their global profile. Local illustrator Liu Qinghua has been recognised at the Shanghai fair, with her work 'Humpback Whale, Going Home!' advancing to the final 50 of the 2026 Golden Windmill International Young Illustrators Contest, run by the Shanghai International Children's Book Fair. The contest drew more than 2,000 entries from 73 countries and regions.
In addition, the Hong Kong pavilion displays works by eight illustrators from the second edition of 'Flying Picture Books', as well as original picture books by 14 Hong Kong and two mainland Chinese illustrators, published under the Cultural and Creative Industries Office-funded 'Hong Kong Picture Book Publishing Support Scheme'. The exhibition aims to introduce publishers from around the world to high-quality Hong Kong picture books.

content:
Megaspeed 表示 Alice Huang 已于 2025 年 8 月离开公司 |中国劳工公告栏
星期一, 16 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
Megaspeed 表示 Alice Huang 已于 2025 年 8 月离开公司
Megaspeed 周日证实，中国女商人 Alice Huang 于 2025 年 8 月 30 日离开这家总部位于新加坡的公司，该公司与英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 的关系引发了美国国家安全担忧。该公司表示，其从事合法业务，并已启动内部调查
总部位于新加坡的 Megaspeed 公司周日表示，中国女商人 Alice Huang 已于 2025 年 8 月 30 日正式离开该公司，并且不再担任该公司的现任职务。此前有媒体报道称黄女士与英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋有关，引发了美国国家安全方面的担忧。
“Megaspeed 对黄女士的个人和私人事务不予置评，”该公司在一份声明中表示。该公司补充说，它知道最近的媒体报道包含有关其业务、供应链和全球运营的断言，但这些断言没有可验证的证据支持。
Megaspeed 表示，其开展了“合法且合法的业务”，并聘请了外部法律顾问来进行彻底的内部调查。
该公司没有提供有关黄女士离职的更多细节，也没有提供媒体报道中提到的国家安全问题的性质。

Megaspeed says Alice Huang left firm in August 2025 | China Labour Bulletin Board
Monday, 16 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Megaspeed says Alice Huang left firm in August 2025
Megaspeed confirmed on Sunday that Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman whose ties to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang raised US national security concerns, left the Singapore-based company on August 30, 2025. The company said it conducted legitimate business and had launched an internal investigation
Singapore-based company Megaspeed said on Sunday that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang had officially left the firm on August 30, 2025, and held no current role there. The announcement came after media reports linked Ms. Huang to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, raising United States national security concerns.
"Megaspeed does not comment on Ms. Huang's personal and private matters," the company said in a statement. It added that it was aware of recent media reports containing assertions about its business, supply chain and global operations that were not supported by verifiable evidence.
Megaspeed said it conducted "legitimate and lawful business" and had retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation.
The company did not provide further details about Ms. Huang's departure or the nature of the national security concerns cited in media reports.

title: Hong Kong police chief stresses privacy safeguards for AI-powered CCTV system
zh_title: 香港警察局长强调人工智能闭路电视系统的隐私保护
summary: 香港警务处长强调人工智能闭路电视系统的隐私保护中国劳工布告栏 星期一，2026 年 11 月 16 日 · 香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 香港警务处长强调人工智能闭路电视系统的隐私保障 警察局长周一鸣表示，警员在使用 SmartView 上新的人工智能面部识别功能之前必须获得批准。他强调了隐私保护，并指出该系统有助于解决严重犯罪和寻找失踪的老年人。警务处处长周一明周日强调，警务人员必须遵守
content:
香港警务处长强调人工智能闭路电视系统的隐私保护中国劳工公告栏
星期一, 16 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
香港警察局长强调人工智能闭路电视系统的隐私保护
警务处处长周一鸣表示，警员在使用 SmartView 上新的人工智能面部识别功能之前必须获得批准。他强调了隐私保护，并指出该系统有助于解决严重犯罪和寻找失踪的老年人。
警务处处长周一鸣周日强调，警务人员必须获得批准才能使用 SmartView 的新人工智能面部识别功能。该功能于周一推出，可自动进行视频分析以支持警方行动。
周在电视节目中表示，有严格的制衡措施以防止滥用。他解释说，只有在调查必要时才会批准人工智能工具。 SmartView 目前在一些购物中心配备了闭路电视摄像头，Chow 表示希望更多组织在了解该系统的用途后加入该网络。
Chow强调了SmartView在打击犯罪方面的作用，称它显着提高了严重犯罪的侦破率。他称赞该系统的视频分析功能有助于解决最近的抢劫案件，并表示它还可以帮助快速识别失踪的患有痴呆症的老年人。
警察局长还提到了施政报告中宣布的无人机集中管理系统，并计划在全市安装 200 个无人机码头。该系统将连接不同的无人机，并允许它们在事件发生时快速部署以支持警察行动。
关于跨境犯罪，周指出香港参与了国际刑警组织于 2025 年启动的银色通缉令试点项目，旨在追踪和定位犯罪资产。香港今年加入了该倡议。他还提到了跨境反诈骗平台FRONTIER+，该平台将帮助与十多个合作地区实施24/7止付机制。
国际刑警组织第94届大会将于11月30日在香港举行。周一岳表示，三年的筹备工作即将结束，并表示对大会取得成功充满信心。他补充说，尽管地缘政治紧张局势日益加剧，世界各地仍希望加强跨境警务合作。由于大会报名仍在进行中，周先生表示，他预计国际刑警组织所有196个成员国和地区的代表都会出席。

Hong Kong police chief stresses privacy safeguards for AI-powered CCTV system | China Labour Bulletin Board
Monday, 16 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong police chief stresses privacy safeguards for AI-powered CCTV system
Police Commissioner Joe Chow Yat-ming said officers must seek approval before using the new AI facial-recognition function on SmartView. He stressed privacy safeguards and noted the system has helped solve serious crimes and find missing elderly people.
Police Commissioner Joe Chow Yat-ming stressed on Sunday that police officers must obtain approval before using SmartView’s new AI facial-recognition function. The feature, which launches Monday, automates video analysis to support police operations.
Speaking on a television programme, Chow said strict checks and balances are in place to prevent misuse. Approval for the AI tool would be granted only when necessary for investigations, he explained. SmartView currently includes CCTV cameras at some shopping malls, and Chow expressed hope that more organisations will join the network once they understand the system’s purpose.
Chow highlighted SmartView’s role in fighting crime, saying it had significantly raised the detection rate for serious offences. He credited the system’s video analysis capabilities with helping solve recent robbery cases, and said it could also aid in the rapid identification of missing elderly individuals with dementia.
The police chief also mentioned a centralised drone-management system announced in the policy address, and plans to install 200 drone docks across the city. The system would connect different drones and allow them to be deployed quickly to support police operations when incidents occur.
On cross-border crime, Chow noted Hong Kong’s participation in INTERPOL’s Silver Notice pilot project, launched in 2025 to track and locate criminal assets. Hong Kong joined the initiative this year. He also referenced FRONTIER+, a cross-border anti-scam platform that will help implement a 24/7 stop-payment mechanism with more than ten partner regions.
The 94th INTERPOL General Assembly will be held in Hong Kong from 30 November. Chow said three years of preparations are coming to an end and expressed confidence that the assembly would be a success. Despite growing geopolitical tensions, regions around the world want to strengthen cross-border police cooperation, he added. As registration for the assembly is still underway, Chow said he expected representatives from all 196 INTERPOL member countries and regions to attend.

zh_title: 出于首都安全担忧，北京禁止拥有无人机
summary: 出于首都安全担忧，北京禁止拥有无人机中国劳工布告栏 星期一，2026 年 11 月 16 日·香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 北京因首都安全担忧而禁止拥有无人机 北京从周日起禁止拥有、储存或运输无人机，以保障首都安全。业主必须通过回购点处置设备或将其移至执法区域之外。反恐、执法、紧急救援、农业可获豁免 北京禁止拥有、储存和运输无人机
content:
出于首都安全担忧，北京禁止拥有无人机中国劳工公告栏
星期一, 16 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
出于首都安全担忧，北京禁止拥有无人机
北京从周日起禁止拥有、储存或运输无人机，以维护首都安全。业主必须通过回购点处置设备或将其移至执法区域之外。反恐、执法、紧急救援、农业等方面可给予豁免
据《旗帜报》报道，北京从周日起禁止拥有、储存和运输无人机，理由是需要“维护首都安全”。
该禁令于 9 月宣布，适用于该市的城乡地区，该市面积约 16,400 平方公里，大约是比利时面积的一半。任何被发现拥有无人机的人都可能面临罚款并没收其设备。
业主被迫在实施日期之前处置他们的设备，要么在批准的回购点转售，要么在网上销售，要么将它们运到执法区域之外。该禁令还禁止将无人机或其组件带入城市。
北京是中国中央政府、最高领导人和执政的中国共产党总部所在地，长期以来一直保持着严格的安全措施。此举是在 6 月份引发空域安全担忧之后做出的，当时一架小型飞机撞上了该市最高的摩天大楼，导致飞行员死亡，另有 13 人受伤。
2026 年 5 月，北京已经禁止无人机销售，要求所有者向当局注册其设备，同时允许他们保留这些设备。最新的规定升级了这些限制。
无人机飞行可能因特定原因而获得豁免，包括反恐、执法、紧急救援、农业或科学研究。报告指出，无人机近年来在中国变得非常受欢迎，特别是在拍摄风景方面。

Beijing bans drone ownership over capital security fears | China Labour Bulletin Board
Monday, 16 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Beijing bans drone ownership over capital security fears
Beijing imposed a ban on owning, storing or transporting drones from Sunday to safeguard the capital's security. Owners had to dispose of devices via buy-back points or move them outside the enforcement area. Exemptions may be granted for counterterrorism, law enforcement, emergency relief, agricult
Beijing imposed a ban on owning, storing and transporting unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) from Sunday, citing the need to “safeguard the security of the capital”, according to a report by The Standard.
The ban, announced in September, applies to both urban and rural areas across the municipality, which covers about 16,400 square kilometres — roughly half the size of Belgium. Anyone found in possession of a drone could face a fine and confiscation of their equipment.
Owners were forced to dispose of their devices ahead of the implementation date, either by reselling them at approved buy-back points, selling them online, or transporting them outside the enforcement area. The ban also prohibits bringing drones or their components into the city.
Beijing, home to China's central government, top leaders and the headquarters of the ruling Chinese Communist Party, has long maintained strict security measures. The move follows airspace safety fears raised in June, when a small plane crashed into the city's tallest skyscraper, killing the pilot and injuring 13 others.
In May 2026, Beijing had already banned drone sales, requiring owners to register their devices with authorities while permitting them to keep them. The latest regulation escalates those restrictions.
Exemptions for drone flights may be granted for specific reasons, including counterterrorism, law enforcement, emergency relief, agriculture or scientific research. Drones have become extremely popular in China in recent years, particularly for filming landscapes, the report noted.

content:
罗姗娜·罗 (Rosanna Law) 称赞“星空交响曲”是具有里程碑意义的年度盛事中国劳工公告栏
星期一, 16 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
罗姗娜·罗 (Rosanna Law) 称赞“星空交响曲”是具有里程碑意义的年度盛事
香港文化局局长称赞这次户外音乐会取得了圆满成功。此次活动以港乐、新任指挥和钢琴家为主角，并配有烟花和光剑。由于天气恶劣，比赛从周五推迟。
文化体育及旅游局局长罗淑佩称赞“星空交响曲”户外音乐会是一次非常成功的里程碑式活动，并指出11月14日星期六晚上场馆爆满。
罗杰周日在社交媒体上发帖称，晴朗的天气和热闹的气氛让与会者可以坐在草地上享受野餐，并在香港管弦乐团（港乐）的表演中欣赏维多利亚港的景色。她强调了观众对乐团新任音乐总监塔尔莫·佩尔托科斯基（Tarmo Peltokoski）和年轻的本地钢琴家岑阿里斯托（Aristo Sham）的巨大期待。
罗指出，今年的节目以轻松、熟悉的经典曲目为各个年龄段的音乐爱好者带来深刻的共鸣，例如圣桑俏皮的《动物嘉年华》，由佩尔托科斯基和岑与多位港乐首席在两架钢琴上演奏。与会者还欣赏了《星球大战组曲》，佩尔托科斯基在乐曲的开头和结尾使用发光的光剑进行了指挥。
晚会以柴可夫斯基1812序曲的表演和壮观的烟花表演结束。由于香港天文台预报有大雨和狂风雷暴，原定于周五举行的音乐会已推迟至周六晚上在中环海滨活动空间举行。

Rosanna Law hails 'Symphony Under the Stars' as landmark annual event
Hong Kong's culture secretary praised the outdoor concert as a packed success. The event featured the HK Phil, a new director and a pianist, with fireworks and a lightsaber. It was postponed from Friday due to bad weather.
Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism Rosanna Law Shuk-pui has hailed the "Symphony Under the Stars" outdoor concert as a highly successful landmark event, noting that the venue was packed to capacity on Saturday night, 14 November.
In a social media post on Sunday, Law said the clear weather and lively atmosphere allowed attendees to sit on the grass, enjoy picnics, and take in views of Victoria Harbour alongside the performance by the Hong Kong Philharmonic Orchestra (HK Phil). She highlighted the immense anticipation from the audience for the orchestra's new music director, Tarmo Peltokoski, and the young local pianist, Aristo Sham.
Law noted that this year's programme featured lighthearted, familiar classics that deeply resonated with music lovers of all ages, such as Saint-Saëns's playful The Carnival of the Animals, which was performed on two pianos by Peltokoski and Sham alongside several HK Phil principals. Attendees also enjoyed the Star Wars Suite, which Peltokoski conducted using a glowing lightsaber at the beginning and end of the piece.
The evening concluded with a performance of Tchaikovsky's 1812 Overture, accompanied by a spectacular fireworks display. The concert, originally scheduled for Friday, had been postponed to Saturday night at the Central Harbourfront Event Space due to the Hong Kong Observatory's forecasts of heavy rain and squally thunderstorms.

当女性步入更年期及停经阶段，血糖就容易上升。（图片来源：siro46/stock.adobe.com） 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
糖尿病，真的只是爱吃甜食、体重过重的人才需要担心吗？国健署最新公布，台湾20岁以上成人糖尿病盛行率达13.1％，平均不到8人就有1人。11月14日世界糖尿病日将至，这个数字对中年女性尤其值得注意。不少人年轻时抽血检查都正常，到了更年期却发现胆固醇升高、腰围变粗，以为只是年纪到了。然而，除了看得见的身材变化，血糖也可能在没有明显症状的情况下悄悄升高。为什么停经前后，连身体控制血糖的能力也可能跟着改变？ 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
鸿馨诊所院长吴佳鸿医师在《别怕荷尔蒙，你抗衰防病的关键》中提醒，血糖的控制在众多退化性慢性疾病、慢性发炎、代谢疾病、心血管疾病、脑部退化、免疫疾病、神经系统疾病，乃至于整体生理机能的衰老中，都扮演了非常关键的角色。因此，步入更年期及停经的中年女性朋友，应该、必须、也值得好好关注自己血糖的变化，千万不要放任它默默升高，无形中对健康造成破坏，也让自己更容易呈现衰老样态。
那么，更年期的荷尔蒙变化对血糖有什么影响呢？你或许猜到了，没错！就跟胆固醇数值及腰围的游泳圈一样，当女性步入更年期及停经阶段，血糖就容易上升。
权威内分泌医学期刊《自然回顾：内分泌学》（Nature Reviews Endocrinology）的一篇探讨女性更年期与糖尿病的研究报告指出，更年期这个过渡期间，年纪增长及雌激素下降，会使女性体内出现许多复杂的生理转变，例如：肌肉量下降、能量消耗减少、胰岛素分泌变化、胰脏分泌胰岛素的β细胞凋亡增加、肝脏代谢胰岛素增加、胰岛素的作用变差、慢性发炎增加、身体活动量减少、腹部脂肪增加、胰岛素阻抗性增加等等。
这些生理变化，都会促使女性罹患糖尿病的风险上升。而糖尿病又容易促使卵巢功能提早衰退，导致女性提早停经；停经又增加这些代谢疾病的风险，可以说是一个恶性循环。最终，这些现象会使得进入更年期或停经的女性，罹患心血管疾病的风险也跟着上升。
既然如此，荷尔蒙补充疗法有助于血糖控制、打破这样的恶性循环吗？答案是：有！以“女性健康促进计划”（WHI）荷尔蒙研究来看，当大家的注意力都放在荷尔蒙与乳癌的议题上时，鲜少人及媒体会再去注意到后续研究透露出来的其他重要讯息。
在女性健康促进计划的雌激素并用黄体素（WHI CEE＋MPA）研究中，针对补充荷尔蒙前3年收集的血糖相关数据进行分析，结果显示，没有罹患糖尿病的女性中，有补充荷尔蒙的组别比起补充安慰剂的组别，罹患糖尿病的风险降低21％，而且胰岛素阻抗性有明显改善。这项研究结果刊登在欧洲糖尿病研究学会（EASD）的官方医学期刊《Diabetologia》。如果分析整个5.6年的荷尔蒙治疗过程，结果依然相同，有补充荷尔蒙的女性，糖尿病风险降低19％。
另一个女性健康促进计划的单用雌激素（WHI CEE）研究也得出了类似的结果，分析整个治疗7.2年的数据，有补充雌激素（CEE）的女性，比补充安慰剂的女性，糖尿病风险降低14％。然而，值得注意的是，后续的追踪发现，停用了荷尔蒙治疗后，无论是单纯补充雌激素（CEE），还是同时补充雌激素（CEE）与黄体素（MPA），这样的好处就消失了。研究结果刊登在《美国医学会杂志》（JAMA）。
一项重要的随机分派双盲安慰剂控制的HERS荷尔蒙研究，针对已罹患冠状动脉心脏病但尚未罹患糖尿病的女性，探讨荷尔蒙补充疗法对血糖及未来糖尿病风险的影响。追踪4.1年的结果显示，使用安慰剂的女性空腹血糖显著上升，而补充荷尔蒙的女性则无此现象；而且，补充荷尔蒙的女性糖尿病发生率较安慰剂组低，风险降低高达35％！该研究结果刊登于《内科医学年监》（Annals of Internal Medicine）。
一份综合了18个随机分派临床试验的统合分析报告也指出，荷尔蒙补充疗法，不论是单纯补充雌激素或合并补充雌激素与黄体素，皆能降低糖尿病风险，但降低幅度因治疗方式而异。该研究报告发表于《美国医学会杂志》（JAMA）。另一个综合了一百多个随机分派临床试验的统合分析报告显示，对于尚未罹患糖尿病的女性，补充荷尔蒙可以降低糖尿病风险；对于已罹患糖尿病的女性，则有助于降低空腹血糖并改善胰岛素阻抗性。
综合各项研究，荷尔蒙补充疗法对糖尿病的影响，我们可以参考国际女性健康机构北美停经学会（NAMS）的官方声明。该组织根据医学研究证据，于2022年修订的荷尔蒙补充疗法声明中，针对糖尿病部分提到以下几个重点，值得女性朋友参考：
◆荷尔蒙疗法有助改善代谢症候群相关指标，并使糖尿病发生率降低高达30％。
◆对于已罹患糖尿病且受到更年期症状困扰的女性，荷尔蒙疗法不仅能缓解更年期症状、改善生活品质，还有助于血糖控制。
◆对于有更年期症状又罹患糖尿病的女性，确实可以考虑使用荷尔蒙补充疗法。然而，荷尔蒙疗法对血糖调控的好处，一旦停止使用荷尔蒙即会消失。
不过，是否适合使用荷尔蒙补充疗法，仍需由医师依年龄、停经时间与个人病史评估，不能仅为了预防糖尿病而自行使用。
（本文节录：《别怕荷尔蒙，你抗衰防病的关键：全面解析更年期症状、心血管健康、失智症、骨质疏松、心理健康、乳癌迷思》一书）
